23.1.59.a.s: ādityaṃ carum / dhenuḥ / vijñāyate ca vatsaṃ pūrvasyāṃ dadāti / mātaram uttarasyā //
23.1.59.a.d: आदित्यं चरुम् । धेनुः । विज्ञायते च वत्सं पूर्वस्यां ददाति । मातरम् उत्तरस्या ॥
23.1.59.a.m: [There is] a mess of boiled grains for Aditi. A milch cow [is the dakṣiṇā]. And it is taught: "He gives a calf at the former [offering], the mother at the latter."

23.1.61.a.m: One desirous of heaven should sacrifice with it.

23.2.1.a.m: One desirous of heaven should pile the Sāvitra [altar].

23.2.3.a.s: ceṣyamāṇa upakalpayate pañcāśītiśatam̐ hiraṇyeṣṭakā yāvad uttamam aṅguliparu tāvatīḥ śarkarā vābhyaktāś catasraḥ svayamātṛṇṇā aparimitā lokaṃpṛṇāḥ //
23.2.3.a.d: चेष्यमाण उपकल्पयते पञ्चाशीतिशतम्̐ हिरण्येष्टका यावद् उत्तमम् अङ्गुलिपरु तावतीः शर्करा वाभ्यक्ताश् चतस्रः स्वयमातृण्णा अपरिमिता लोकंपृणाः ॥
23.2.3.a.m: One intending to pile [it] procures one hundred and eighty-five gold bricks, or pebbles of the size of the top finger-joint smeared with butter, four naturally perforated bricks, and an unlimited number of space-filling bricks.

23.2.4.a.s: ṣaḍḍhotāram ity etadādi pāśukam karma pratipadyate //
23.2.4.a.d: षड्ढोतारम् इत्य् एतदादि पाशुकम् कर्म प्रतिपद्यते ॥
23.2.4.a.m: He begins the animal rite beginning with: "[He offers] the six-hotṛ oblation...".

23.2.5.a.m: It is taught: "He should sacrifice on the third part of the altar."

23.2.6.a.s: prāg uttarasmāt parigrahāt kṛtvottaravedideśasya madhye śaṅkuṃ nihatya sarvataḥ parimaṇḍalaṃ rathacakramātraṃ sāvitraṃ parilikhya samūlaṃ haritaṃ darbhastambam āhṛtya madhye 'gner nikhāya juhvāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sajūr abdo 'yāvabhir iti darbhastambe pañcāhutīr hutvoddhatyāvokṣya vyāghāraṇāntām uttaravediṃ kṛtvā lekhāyā abhyantaraṃ nava parimaṇḍalā lekhā likhitvā sikatābhir avakīrya darbhaiḥ pracchādya dadhnā madhumiśreṇa śarkarābhir iti bāhyāṃ lekhāṃ saṃpūrya vasati //
23.2.6.a.d: प्राग् उत्तरस्मात् परिग्रहात् कृत्वोत्तरवेदिदेशस्य मध्ये शङ्कुं निहत्य सर्वतः परिमण्डलं रथचक्रमात्रं सावित्रं परिलिख्य समूलं हरितं दर्भस्तम्बम् आहृत्य मध्ये ऽग्नेर् निखाय जुह्वां पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वा सजूर् अब्दो ऽयावभिर् इति दर्भस्तम्बे पञ्चाहुतीर् हुत्वोद्धत्यावोक्ष्य व्याघारणान्ताम् उत्तरवेदिं कृत्वा लेखाया अभ्यन्तरं नव परिमण्डला लेखा लिखित्वा सिकताभिर् अवकीर्य दर्भैः प्रच्छाद्य दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण शर्कराभिर् इति बाह्यां लेखां संपूर्य वसति ॥
23.2.6.a.m: Having performed [the work] up to the second tracing of the altar boundaries, having driven in a peg in the center of the site of the high altar, having traced out in a circle on all sides the Sāvitra [altar] of the size of a chariot wheel, having brought a green clump of darbha grass with its roots, having buried it in the middle of the fire[-site], having taken five ladlings [of clarified butter] in the juhū ladle, having offered five oblations onto the darbha clump with: "United with the year, with the half-months...", having excavated [it], having sprinkled [it] with water, having completed the high altar up to the cross-sprinkling, having drawn nine circular furrows within the [outer] line, having strewn them with sand, having covered them with darbha grass, having filled the outer furrow with curd mixed with honey and with pebbles, he waits overnight.

23.2.7.a.s: hute 'gnihotre prajāpatis tvā sādayatu \ tayā devatayāṅgirasvad dhruvā sīda \\ ity uttaravedim abhimṛśya mayi gṛhṇāmi \ yo no agnir iti dvābhyām ātmann agniṃ gṛhītvā yās te agne samidhas \\ iti svayaṃcityābhimṛśya \\ agner bhasmāsi \\ iti sikatā nivapati / saṃjñānam ity ūṣān //
23.2.7.a.d: हुते ऽग्निहोत्रे प्रजापतिस् त्वा सादयतु \ तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवा सीद \\ इत्य् उत्तरवेदिम् अभिमृश्य मयि गृह्णामि \ यो नो अग्निर् इति द्वाभ्याम् आत्मन्न् अग्निं गृहीत्वा यास् ते अग्ने समिधस् \\ इति स्वयंचित्याभिमृश्य \\ अग्नेर् भस्मासि \\ इति सिकता निवपति । संज्ञानम् इत्य् ऊषान् ॥
23.2.7.a.m: When the Agnihotra has been offered, having touched the high altar with: "May Prajāpati seat you; with that deity, Angiras-like, sit firm!", having taken the fire into himself with the two [mantras]: "In myself I take..." [and] "The fire that is within us...", having touched the self-piling [bricks] with: "The kindling-sticks that are yours, O Agni...", he scatters sand with: "You are the ashes of Agni"; [and] saline earth with: "Mutual understanding...".

23.2.8.a.s: tān nivapan yad adaś candramasi kṛṣṇaṃ tad ihāstu \\ iti manasā dhyāyati //
23.2.8.a.d: तान् निवपन् यद् अदश् चन्द्रमसि कृष्णं तद् इहास्तु \\ इति मनसा ध्यायति ॥
23.2.8.a.m: Scattering them, he meditates in his mind: "What is black over there in the moon, let that be here."

23.2.9.a.s: saṃ yā vaḥ priyās tanuvas \\ ity ūṣān sikatāś ca sam̐sṛjya citaḥ stha paricitas \\ ity aparimitābhiḥ śarkarābhiḥ pariśritya \\ āpyāyasva sametu te \\ iti sikatā vyūhati //
23.2.9.a.d: सं या वः प्रियास् तनुवस् \\ इत्य् ऊषान् सिकताश् च सम्̐सृज्य चितः स्थ परिचितस् \\ इत्य् अपरिमिताभिः शर्कराभिः परिश्रित्य \\ आप्यायस्व समेतु ते \\ इति सिकता व्यूहति ॥
23.2.9.a.m: Having mixed the saline earth and the sand with: "The dear bodies of yours that are united...", having enclosed [it] with an unlimited number of pebbles with: "You are piled, you are enclosed...", he spreads out the sand with: "Swell up, let [vitality] come together to you...".

23.2.10.a.m: He does not confuse the furrows.

23.2.11.a.s: abhyantaraṃ jaghanārdha udapātram upadadhāti vāk tvā samudra upadadhāmi suprajāvanim̐ rāyaspoṣavaniṃ mahyaṃ vājināya \\ iti //
23.2.11.a.d: अभ्यन्तरं जघनार्ध उदपात्रम् उपदधाति वाक् त्वा समुद्र उपदधामि सुप्रजावनिम्̐ रायस्पोषवनिं मह्यं वाजिनाय \\ इति ॥
23.2.11.a.m: In the interior, in the western half, he places a water vessel with: "Speech, the ocean, I place you, winning good offspring, winning abundance of wealth for me, the swift runner."

23.2.12.a.s: navamyāṃ bāhyāyāṃ lekhāyāṃ pañcadaśa pūrvapakṣasyāhāny upadadhāti // saṃjñānam \\ vijñānam iti //
23.2.12.a.d: नवम्यां बाह्यायां लेखायां पञ्चदश पूर्वपक्षस्याहान्य् उपदधाति ॥ संज्ञानम् \\ विज्ञानम् इति ॥
23.2.12.a.m: In the ninth, outer furrow, he places [bricks representing] the fifteen days of the waxing half of the month, with: "Understanding...", "Distinct knowledge...".

23.2.13.a.s: teṣām antarāleṣv eteṣām ahnāṃ pañcadaśa muhūrtān upadadhāti citraḥ \ ketur iti //
23.2.13.a.d: तेषाम् अन्तरालेष्व् एतेषाम् अह्नां पञ्चदश मुहूर्तान् उपदधाति चित्रः \ केतुर् इति ॥
23.2.13.a.m: In their intervals, he places the fifteen muhūrtas of these days with [the formulas], 'citraḥ ketuḥ...'.

23.2.14.a.s: athāntarasyāṃ pañcadaśa pūrvapakṣasya rātrīr upadadhāti darśā \ dṛṣṭā \\ iti //
23.2.14.a.d: अथान्तरस्यां पञ्चदश पूर्वपक्षस्य रात्रीर् उपदधाति दर्शा \ दृष्टा \\ इति ॥
23.2.14.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the fifteen nights of the waxing fortnight with, 'darśā dṛṣṭā...'.

23.2.15.a.s: tāsām antarāleṣv etāsāṃ rātrīṇāṃ pañcadaśa muhūrtān upadadhāti dātā \ pradātā \\ iti //
23.2.15.a.d: तासाम् अन्तरालेष्व् एतासां रात्रीणां पञ्चदश मुहूर्तान् उपदधाति दाता \ प्रदाता \\ इति ॥
23.2.15.a.m: In their intervals, he places the fifteen muhūrtas of these nights with, 'dātā pradātā...'.

23.2.16.a.s: athāntarasyāṃ pañcadaśāparapakṣasyāhāny upadadhāti prastutam \\ viṣṭutam iti //
23.2.16.a.d: अथान्तरस्यां पञ्चदशापरपक्षस्याहान्य् उपदधाति प्रस्तुतम् \\ विष्टुतम् इति ॥
23.2.16.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the fifteen days of the waning fortnight with, 'prastutam viṣṭutam...'.

23.2.17.a.s: teṣām antarāleṣv eteṣām ahnāṃ pañcadaśa muhūrtān upadadhāti savitā \ prasavitā \\ iti //
23.2.17.a.d: तेषाम् अन्तरालेष्व् एतेषाम् अह्नां पञ्चदश मुहूर्तान् उपदधाति सविता \ प्रसविता \\ इति ॥
23.2.17.a.m: In their intervals, he places the fifteen muhūrtas of these days with, 'savitā prasavitā...'.

23.2.18.a.s: athāntarasyāṃ pañcadaśāparapakṣasya rātrīr upadadhāti sutā \ sunvatī \\ iti //
23.2.18.a.d: अथान्तरस्यां पञ्चदशापरपक्षस्य रात्रीर् उपदधाति सुता \ सुन्वती \\ इति ॥
23.2.18.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the fifteen nights of the waning fortnight with, 'sutā sunvatī...'.

23.2.19.a.s: tāsām antarāleṣv etāsām rātrīṇāṃ pañcadaśa muhūrtān upadadhāti \\ abhiśāstā \\ anumantā \\ iti //
23.2.19.a.d: तासाम् अन्तरालेष्व् एतासाम् रात्रीणां पञ्चदश मुहूर्तान् उपदधाति \\ अभिशास्ता \\ अनुमन्ता \\ इति ॥
23.2.19.a.m: In their intervals, he places the fifteen muhūrtas of these nights with, 'abhiśāstā anumantā...'.

23.2.20.a.s: athāntarasyāṃ dvādaśa pūrvapakṣān upadadhāti pavitram \\ pavayiṣyan \\ iti //
23.2.20.a.d: अथान्तरस्यां द्वादश पूर्वपक्षान् उपदधाति पवित्रम् \\ पवयिष्यन् \\ इति ॥
23.2.20.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the twelve waxing fortnights with, 'pavitram pavayiṣyan...'.

23.2.21.a.s: athāntarasyām dvādaśāparapakṣān upadadhāti sahasvān \ sahīyān iti //
23.2.21.a.d: अथान्तरस्याम् द्वादशापरपक्षान् उपदधाति सहस्वान् \ सहीयान् इति ॥
23.2.21.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the twelve waning fortnights with, 'sahasvān sahīyān...'.

23.2.22.a.s: athāntarasyāṃ trayodaśa māsanāmāny upadadhāti \\ aruṇas \\ aruṇarajās \\ iti //
23.2.22.a.d: अथान्तरस्यां त्रयोदश मासनामान्य् उपदधाति \\ अरुणस् \\ अरुणरजास् \\ इति ॥
23.2.22.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the names of the thirteen months with, 'aruṇaḥ aruṇarajāḥ...'.

23.2.23.a.s: atha sikatā upadadhāti \\ ejatkā jovatkās \\ iti //
23.2.23.a.d: अथ सिकता उपदधाति \\ एजत्का जोवत्कास् \\ इति ॥
23.2.23.a.m: Then he places the sand with, 'ejatkā jovatkāḥ...'.

23.2.24.a.s: athāntarasyāṃ pañcadaśa muhūrtān upadadhāti idānīm \\ tadānīm iti //
23.2.24.a.d: अथान्तरस्यां पञ्चदश मुहूर्तान् उपदधाति इदानीम् \\ तदानीम् इति ॥
23.2.24.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the fifteen muhūrtas with, 'idānīm tadānīm...'.

23.2.25.a.s: athāntarasyāṃ ṣaḍ yajñakratūm̐s trīṇi caturnāmany upadadhāti \\ agniṣṭomas \\ ukthyas \\ agnir ṛtur iti //
23.2.25.a.d: अथान्तरस्यां षड् यज्ञक्रतूम्̐स् त्रीणि चतुर्नामन्य् उपदधाति \\ अग्निष्टोमस् \\ उक्थ्यस् \\ अग्निर् ऋतुर् इति ॥
23.2.25.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the six sacrificial rites [and] the three fourfold names with, 'agniṣṭomaḥ ukthyaḥ... agnir ṛtuḥ...'.

23.2.26.a.s: atha nābhyāṃ catvāri saṃvatsaranāmāny upadadhāti prajāpatiḥ \ saṃvatsaras \\ mahān \ kas \\ iti //
23.2.26.a.d: अथ नाभ्यां चत्वारि संवत्सरनामान्य् उपदधाति प्रजापतिः \ संवत्सरस् \\ महान् \ कस् \\ इति ॥
23.2.26.a.m: Then in the navel, he places the four names of the year with, 'prajāpatiḥ saṃvatsaraḥ mahān kaḥ...'.

23.2.27.a.s: catasraḥ svayamātṛṇṇā dikṣūpadadhāti bhūr agniṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca māṃ ca \\ iti //
23.2.27.a.d: चतस्रः स्वयमातृण्णा दिक्षूपदधाति भूर् अग्निं च पृथिवीं च मां च \\ इति ॥
23.2.27.a.m: He places four naturally perforated stones in the cardinal directions with, 'bhūr agniṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca māṃ ca...'.

23.2.29.a.s: cātvālāt purīṣam āhṛtya pṛṣṭo divi \\ iti vaiśvānaryarcā citāv anuvyūhati //
23.2.29.a.d: चात्वालात् पुरीषम् आहृत्य पृष्टो दिवि \\ इति वैश्वानर्यर्चा चिताव् अनुव्यूहति ॥
23.2.29.a.m: Having brought loose earth from the pit, he scatters it over the layer with the verse to Vaiśvānara, 'pṛṣṭo divi...'.

23.2.31.a.m: He mutters the ascending formula; he mutters the descending formula.

23.2.32.a.s: upasthānenopatiṣṭhate tvam eva tvāṃ vettha yo 'si so 'si \\ iti //
23.2.32.a.d: उपस्थानेनोपतिष्ठते त्वम् एव त्वां वेत्थ यो ऽसि सो ऽसि \\ इति ॥
23.2.32.a.m: He reverences [it] with the attendance verse, 'tvam eva tvāṃ vettha yo 'si so 'si...'.

23.2.34.a.s: dhenūḥ kṛtvā yajamānaḥ saṃhāravihārābhyām upatiṣṭhate saṃvatsaro 'si \ parivatsaro 'si \\ iti //
23.2.34.a.d: धेनूः कृत्वा यजमानः संहारविहाराभ्याम् उपतिष्ठते संवत्सरो ऽसि \ परिवत्सरो ऽसि \\ इति ॥
23.2.34.a.m: Having formed the milk cows, the sacrificer attends upon [them] with the drawing-together and scattering [movements] with, 'saṃvatsaro 'si parivatsaro 'si...'.

23.2.35.a.m: On the northern side, on the highest brick, he offers goat's milk with a calotropis leaf.

23.2.36.a.s: tvam agne rudras \\ iti śatarudrīyasya rūpam asaṃcare paśūnām arkaparṇa udasyati valmīkavapāyāṃ vāvadadhāti //
23.2.36.a.d: त्वम् अग्ने रुद्रस् \\ इति शतरुद्रीयस्य रूपम् असंचरे पशूनाम् अर्कपर्ण उदस्यति वल्मीकवपायां वावदधाति ॥
23.2.36.a.m: With the formula representing the Śatarudrīya, 'tvam agne rudraḥ...', he throws away the calotropis leaf in a place where cattle do not roam, or he inserts it into an anthill.

23.2.37.a.s: jaghanenāgniṃ prāṅmukha upaviśya saṃcitokthyena hotānuśaṃsati bhūr bhuvaḥ svar ity anuvākena //
23.2.37.a.d: जघनेनाग्निं प्राङ्मुख उपविश्य संचितोक्थ्येन होतानुशंसति भूर् भुवः स्वर् इत्य् अनुवाकेन ॥
23.2.37.a.m: Sitting down behind the fire facing east, the hotṛ recites along with the piled-up ukthya [verses] by means of the section, 'bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ...'.

23.2.38.a.s: agnipraṇayanādi pāśukaṃ karma pratipadyate samānam ātimuktībhyaḥ //
23.2.38.a.d: अग्निप्रणयनादि पाशुकं कर्म प्रतिपद्यते समानम् आतिमुक्तीभ्यः ॥
23.2.38.a.m: He proceeds with the animal sacrificial rite beginning with the bringing forward of the fire, identically up to the Atimukti offerings.

23.2.39.a.s: atimuktīr hutvā caturgṛhītaṃ juhoti tvam agne rudras iti śatarudrīyasya rūpam //
23.2.39.a.d: अतिमुक्तीर् हुत्वा चतुर्गृहीतं जुहोति त्वम् अग्ने रुद्रस् इति शतरुद्रीयस्य रूपम् ॥
23.2.39.a.m: Having offered the Atimukti offerings, he offers a fourfold ladleful [of clarified butter], which is the form of the Śatarudrīya, with 'tvam agne rudraḥ...'.

23.2.40.a.s: aparaṃ caturgṛhītam agnāviṣṇū iti vasor dhārāyāḥ / aparaṃ caturgṛhītam annapate \\ ity annahomaḥ / aparaṃ caturgṛhītam \\ sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvās \\ iti viśvaprīḥ / aparaṃ caturgṛhītam // vasūnāṃ tvādhītena rudrāṇām ūrmyādityānāṃ tejasā viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ kratunā marutām emnā juhomi svāhā \\ iti //
23.2.40.a.d: अपरं चतुर्गृहीतम् अग्नाविष्णू इति वसोर् धारायाः । अपरं चतुर्गृहीतम् अन्नपते \\ इत्य् अन्नहोमः । अपरं चतुर्गृहीतम् \\ सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वास् \\ इति विश्वप्रीः । अपरं चतुर्गृहीतम् ॥ वसूनां त्वाधीतेन रुद्राणाम् ऊर्म्यादित्यानां तेजसा विश्वेषां देवानां क्रतुना मरुताम् एम्ना जुहोमि स्वाहा \\ इति ॥
23.2.40.a.m: Another fourfold ladleful with 'agnāviṣṇū...' for the Vasordhārā; another fourfold ladleful with 'annapate...' as the food offering; another fourfold ladleful with 'sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvāḥ...' as the all-satisfying offering; another fourfold ladleful with 'vasūnāṃ tvādhītena rudrāṇām ūrmyādityānāṃ tejasā viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ kratunā marutām emnā juhomi svāhā'.

23.2.41.a.s: tāsāṃ sam̐srāveṇa yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe rājñī virājñī \\ ity anuvākena //
23.2.41.a.d: तासां सम्̐स्रावेण यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे राज्ञी विराज्ञी \\ इत्य् अनुवाकेन ॥
23.2.41.a.m: With the residue of those [offerings], the sacrificer wipes his face with the section, 'rājñī virājñī...'.

23.2.42.a.s: athaikavim̐śatim āhutīr juhoti \\ asave svāhā vasave svāhā \\ ity anuvākena pratimantram //
23.2.42.a.d: अथैकविम्̐शतिम् आहुतीर् जुहोति \\ असवे स्वाहा वसवे स्वाहा \\ इत्य् अनुवाकेन प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
23.2.42.a.m: Then he offers twenty-one oblations, formula by formula with the section, 'asave svāhā vasave svāhā...'.

23.2.43.a.s: barhiṣaḥ saṃbharaṇādi pāśukaṃ karma pratipadyate / samānam ā vapāyā homāt //
23.2.43.a.d: बर्हिषः संभरणादि पाशुकं कर्म प्रतिपद्यते । समानम् आ वपाया होमात् ॥
23.2.43.a.m: He proceeds with the animal sacrificial rite beginning with the gathering of sacred grass, identically up to the offering of the omentum.

23.2.44.a.s: hutāyāṃ vapāyām anviṣṭakaṃ paṣṭhauhīr dakṣiṇā dadāti //
23.2.44.a.d: हुतायां वपायाम् अन्विष्टकं पष्ठौहीर् दक्षिणा ददाति ॥
23.2.44.a.m: When the omentum has been offered, he gives four-year-old heifers as sacrificial gifts according to each brick.

23.2.45.a.s: yady etāvatīr dakṣiṇā notsaheta manthān etāvataḥ / pāyayed brāhmaṇān / odanān vāśayet //
23.2.45.a.d: यद्य् एतावतीर् दक्षिणा नोत्सहेत मन्थान् एतावतः । पाययेद् ब्राह्मणान् । ओदनान् वाशयेत् ॥
23.2.45.a.m: If he cannot afford so many sacrificial gifts, he should make brāhmaṇas drink that many churned beverages, or feed [them] boiled rice.

23.2.46.a.s: tena haivāsya sa kāma upāpto bhavati //
23.2.46.a.d: तेन हैवास्य स काम उपाप्तो भवति ॥
23.2.46.a.m: By that indeed that desire of his becomes attained.

23.2.47.a.s: yat prāṅ manotāyās tat kṛtvaudumbarapātreṇa yūṣṇo mṛtyave grahaṃ gṛhṇāti vipaścite pavamānāya \\ iti grahaṇasādanau / nāciketa eva mṛtyugraha ity eke
23.2.47.a.d: यत् प्राङ् मनोतायास् तत् कृत्वौदुम्बरपात्रेण यूष्णो मृत्यवे ग्रहं गृह्णाति विपश्चिते पवमानाय \\ इति ग्रहणसादनौ । नाचिकेत एव मृत्युग्रह इत्य् एके
23.2.47.a.m: Having done whatever comes before the manotā [verse], he draws a cupful of broth for Mṛtyu with a vessel of udumbara wood, with 'vipaścite pavamānāya...' as the drawing and depositing formulas; some say that the cup for Mṛtyu belongs only to the Nāciketa [fire].

23.2.48.a.m: Its offering takes place after the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

23.2.49.a.s: hoṣyann apa upaspṛśet \\ vidyud asi \ vidya me pāpmānam iti / atha juhoti \\ apa mṛtyum apa kṣudham iti //
23.2.49.a.d: होष्यन्न् अप उपस्पृशेत् \\ विद्युद् असि \ विद्य मे पाप्मानम् इति । अथ जुहोति \\ अप मृत्युम् अप क्षुधम् इति ॥
23.2.49.a.m: About to offer, he should touch water with, 'vidyud asi vidya me pāpmānam...'; then he offers with, 'apa mṛtyum apa kṣudham...'.

23.2.50.a.s: atha hutvopaspṛśet \\ vṛṣṭir asi \ vṛśca me pāpmānam iti / tasyeḍām anu bhakṣaḥ / bhakṣayati bhakṣo 'sy amṛtabhakṣas \\ iti / bhakṣayitvā prāṇanivahān ātman pratiṣṭhāpayate mandrābhibhūtir ity anuvākaśeṣeṇa / samānam ata ūrdhvaṃ pāśukaṃ karma / saṃtiṣṭhate sāvitraḥ //
23.2.50.a.d: अथ हुत्वोपस्पृशेत् \\ वृष्टिर् असि \ वृश्च मे पाप्मानम् इति । तस्येडाम् अनु भक्षः । भक्षयति भक्षो ऽस्य् अमृतभक्षस् \\ इति । भक्षयित्वा प्राणनिवहान् आत्मन् प्रतिष्ठापयते मन्द्राभिभूतिर् इत्य् अनुवाकशेषेण । समानम् अत ऊर्ध्वं पाशुकं कर्म । संतिष्ठते सावित्रः ॥
23.2.50.a.m: Then, having offered, he should touch [water] with, 'vṛṣṭir asi vṛśca me pāpmānam...'; its consumption takes place after the iḍā; he consumes it with, 'bhakṣo 'sy amṛtabhakṣaḥ...'; having consumed it, he establishes the vital breaths within himself with the remainder of the section, 'mandrābhibhūtiḥ...'; from then on, the animal sacrificial rite is identical; the Sāvitra [fire-piling] is completed.

23.3.1.a.s: etena nāciketo vyākhyātaḥ / nātra lekhā bhavanti / ekavim̐śatir hiraṇyeṣṭakāḥ śarkarā vābhyaktā upadhānakāle nābhyām evopadhīyante caturaśraṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ vā loko 'si svargo 'si \\ ity anuvākena pratimantram //
23.3.1.a.d: एतेन नाचिकेतो व्याख्यातः । नात्र लेखा भवन्ति । एकविम्̐शतिर् हिरण्येष्टकाः शर्करा वाभ्यक्ता उपधानकाले नाभ्याम् एवोपधीयन्ते चतुरश्रं परिमण्डलं वा लोको ऽसि स्वर्गो ऽसि \\ इत्य् अनुवाकेन प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
23.3.1.a.m: By this the Nāciketa is explained; here there are no furrows; twenty-one golden bricks or smeared pebbles are placed right in the navel at the time of placement, whether square or circular, formula by formula with the section, 'loko 'si svargo 'si...'.

23.3.2.a.s: tam̐ hy eke paśubandha evottaravedyāṃ cinvata iti brāhmaṇavyākhyātāḥ kāmyā vikārāḥ //
23.3.2.a.d: तम्̐ ह्य् एके पशुबन्ध एवोत्तरवेद्यां चिन्वत इति ब्राह्मणव्याख्याताः काम्या विकाराः ॥
23.3.2.a.m: For some pile it only in an animal sacrifice upon the high altar; thus the optional modifications are explained by the Brāhmaṇa.

23.3.4.a.s: paśubandhe some satre sahasre sarvavedase vā yatra vā bhūyiṣṭhā āhutayo hūyeram̐s tatra cetavyaḥ //
23.3.4.a.d: पशुबन्धे सोमे सत्रे सहस्रे सर्ववेदसे वा यत्र वा भूयिष्ठा आहुतयो हूयेरम्̐स् तत्र चेतव्यः ॥
23.3.4.a.m: In an animal sacrifice, in a Soma sacrifice, in a sattra, in a thousand-[cow sacrifice], or in an all-property sacrifice, or wherever the greatest number of oblations would be offered, there it should be piled.

23.3.5.a.s: satre pratiṣṭhāṃ prajāṃ paśūn svargam ṛddhim īpsan yathāvakāśaṃ yathāsamāmnātam //
23.3.5.a.d: सत्रे प्रतिष्ठां प्रजां पशून् स्वर्गम् ऋद्धिम् ईप्सन् यथावकाशं यथासमाम्नातम् ॥
23.3.5.a.m: Desiring stability in a sattra, offspring, cattle, heaven, [or] prosperity, [he piles it] according to the occasion, as handed down in the sacred tradition.

23.3.6.a.d: सर्वत्र पुरस्ताद् उपक्रमः प्रदक्षिणम् उत्तरतो ऽपवर्गः ॥
23.3.6.a.m: In all cases, the beginning is in the east, [proceeding] sunwise, and the completion is in the north.

23.3.7.a.s: paśukāmaḥ pāṅktam eva cinvīta / pañcapañca pratidiśam ekāṃ madhye //
23.3.7.a.d: पशुकामः पाङ्क्तम् एव चिन्वीत । पञ्चपञ्च प्रतिदिशम् एकां मध्ये ॥
23.3.7.a.m: One desiring cattle should pile a fivefold one: five in each direction, one in the middle.

23.3.8.a.s: jyaiṣṭhyam īpsan yaśaḥ prajāṃ vā trivṛtam eva / sapta purastāt tisro dakṣiṇataḥ sapta paścāt tisra uttarata ekāṃ madhye //
23.3.8.a.d: ज्यैष्ठ्यम् ईप्सन् यशः प्रजां वा त्रिवृतम् एव । सप्त पुरस्तात् तिस्रो दक्षिणतः सप्त पश्चात् तिस्र उत्तरत एकां मध्ये ॥
23.3.8.a.m: Desiring pre-eminence, fame, or offspring, [he should pile] a threefold one: seven in the east, three in the south, seven in the west, three in the north, [and] one in the middle.

23.3.9.a.m: One desiring pre-eminence, starting from the middle, should lay an upward line.

23.3.10.a.s: svargakāmaḥ paścāt prakramya prācīṃ rītiṃ pratipādayet //
23.3.10.a.d: स्वर्गकामः पश्चात् प्रक्रम्य प्राचीं रीतिं प्रतिपादयेत् ॥
23.3.10.a.m: One desiring heaven, starting from the west, should lay an eastward line.

23.3.11.a.s: sa yadīcchet tejasvī yaśasvī brahmavarcasī syām iti prāg dakṣiṇebhyaḥ prāṅ ā hotur dhiṣṇyād utsarpet \\ yeyaṃ prāgād yaśasvatī sā mā prorṇotu tejasā yaśasā brahmavarcasena \\ iti
23.3.11.a.d: स यदीच्छेत् तेजस्वी यशस्वी ब्रह्मवर्चसी स्याम् इति प्राग् दक्षिणेभ्यः प्राङ् आ होतुर् धिष्ण्याद् उत्सर्पेत् \\ येयं प्रागाद् यशस्वती सा मा प्रोर्णोतु तेजसा यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन \\ इति
23.3.11.a.m: If he should desire, 'May I be full of fiery energy, famous, and endowed with spiritual lustre', he should glide forward before the sacrificial gifts, forward up to the hearth of the hotṛ, with: 'May this glorious one that has come forth in the east envelope me with fiery energy, fame, and spiritual lustre'.

23.3.12.a.s: atha yadīcched bhūyiṣṭhaṃ me śraddadhīran bhūyiṣṭhā dakṣiṇā nayeyur iti dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu prācy ehi prācy ehi \\ iti //
23.3.12.a.d: अथ यदीच्छेद् भूयिष्ठं मे श्रद्दधीरन् भूयिष्ठा दक्षिणा नयेयुर् इति दक्षिणासु नीयमानासु प्राच्य् एहि प्राच्य् एहि \\ इति ॥
23.3.12.a.m: Then if he should desire, 'May they trust me most, may they lead the most sacrificial gifts', he [recites] while the sacrificial gifts are being led, 'Come eastward, come eastward...'.

23.3.13.a.s: prācī juṣāṇā vetv ājyasya svāhā \\ iti sruveṇopahatyāhavanīye juhuyāt //
23.3.13.a.d: प्राची जुषाणा वेत्व् आज्यस्य स्वाहा \\ इति स्रुवेणोपहत्याहवनीये जुहुयात् ॥
23.3.13.a.m: With the mantra, 'May she, turned toward the east, enjoying it, partake of the clarified butter, svāhā,' having scooped up with the dipping spoon, he should offer into the āhavanīya fire.

23.3.14.a.m: Beginning with the naturally perforated [brick], the rest is identical.

23.3.16.a.m: By this, the Cāturhotra fire-altar is explained.

23.3.17.a.m: There are as many gold bricks, or anointing pebbles, as there are pādas [in the mantras].

23.3.18.a.s: upadhānakāle 'greṇa darbhastambaṃ daśahotāraṃ pratimantram udañcam upadadhāti / hṛdayaṃ grahaṃ catvāri padāni saṃbhārāṇāṃ dve patnīnām //
23.3.18.a.d: उपधानकाले ऽग्रेण दर्भस्तम्बं दशहोतारं प्रतिमन्त्रम् उदञ्चम् उपदधाति । हृदयं ग्रहं चत्वारि पदानि संभाराणां द्वे पत्नीनाम् ॥
23.3.18.a.m: At the time of piling, in front of a clump of darbha-grass, he lays down the Daśahotṛ mantra to the north, mantra by mantra: the 'heart', the 'cup', four quarters of the materials, and two of the wives.

23.3.19.a.s: evaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ prāñcaṃ caturhotāram / paścād udañcaṃ pañcahotāram / uttarataḥ prāñcaṃ ṣaḍḍhotāram / upariṣṭāt prāñcaṃ saptahotāram / pañcātra padāni saṃbhārāṇām avaśiṣṭāni ca patnīnām //
23.3.19.a.d: एवं दक्षिणतः प्राञ्चं चतुर्होतारम् । पश्चाद् उदञ्चं पञ्चहोतारम् । उत्तरतः प्राञ्चं षड्ढोतारम् । उपरिष्टात् प्राञ्चं सप्तहोतारम् । पञ्चात्र पदानि संभाराणाम् अवशिष्टानि च पत्नीनाम् ॥
23.3.19.a.m: In the same manner, [he lays down] the Caturhotṛ to the south, facing east; the Pañcahotṛ behind, facing north; the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ to the north, facing east; the Saptahotṛ above, facing east; here, there are five quarters of the materials, and the remaining ones belong to the wives.

23.3.20.a.m: Beginning with the naturally perforated [brick], the rest is identical.

23.3.22.a.m: By this, the Vaiśvasṛja fire-altar is explained.

23.3.23.a.s: yāvan mantram̐ hiraṇyeṣṭakā yāvad uttamam aṅguliparu tāvatīḥ śarkarā vābhyaktāś catasraḥ svayamātṛṇṇāḥ //
23.3.23.a.d: यावन् मन्त्रम्̐ हिरण्येष्टका यावद् उत्तमम् अङ्गुलिपरु तावतीः शर्करा वाभ्यक्ताश् चतस्रः स्वयमातृण्णाः ॥
23.3.23.a.m: There are as many gold bricks as there are mantras, or as many anointing pebbles as the last finger-joint, and four naturally perforated [bricks].

23.3.24.a.s: upadhānakāle 'greṇottaranābhim \\ yac cāmṛtaṃ yac ca martyam ity etais tribhir anuvākair triḥ pradakṣiṇam uttaravediṃ paricinoti //
23.3.24.a.d: उपधानकाले ऽग्रेणोत्तरनाभिम् \\ यच् चामृतं यच् च मर्त्यम् इत्य् एतैस् त्रिभिर् अनुवाकैर् त्रिः प्रदक्षिणम् उत्तरवेदिं परिचिनोति ॥
23.3.24.a.m: At the time of piling, in front of the navel of the high altar, with these three anuvākas beginning 'Whatever is immortal and whatever is mortal,' he piles up around the high altar three times in a clockwise direction.

23.3.25.a.m: Or [there are] three layers with the three anuvākas.

23.3.26.a.s: ṛcāṃ prācī mahatī \\ iti saṃcitokthyena hotānuśam̐sati //
23.3.26.a.d: ऋचां प्राची महती \\ इति संचितोक्थ्येन होतानुशम्̐सति ॥
23.3.26.a.m: With the ukthya-chant [beginning] 'The eastern great one of verses,' the hotṛ recites after [the piling] is complete.

23.3.27.a.s: svayamātṛṇṇādi samānam uttaram / śatarātre sārasvateṣu rātrisatreṣu śatarātrānteṣu mahāvrateṣu triṣu ca sārasvateṣu satreṣu kāṭhakacāturmāsyeṣu sādhyānāṃ ṣaḍahavarjiteṣu viśvasṛjāmayane prajāpater anyatrānuśam̐sanāt //
23.3.27.a.d: स्वयमातृण्णादि समानम् उत्तरम् । शतरात्रे सारस्वतेषु रात्रिसत्रेषु शतरात्रान्तेषु महाव्रतेषु त्रिषु च सारस्वतेषु सत्रेषु काठकचातुर्मास्येषु साध्यानां षडहवर्जितेषु विश्वसृजामयने प्रजापतेर् अन्यत्रानुशम्̐सनात् ॥
23.3.27.a.m: Beginning with the naturally perforated [brick], the rest is identical; [this applies] in the Śatarātra, in the Sārasvata night-sessions, in the Mahāvrata rites at the end of the Śatarātra, in the three Sārasvata sattra-sessions, in the Kāṭhaka four-month sacrifices, [in the sessions] of the Sādhyas excluding the six-day rite, and in the Viśvasṛjām Ayana, except for the recitation after [the piling] of Prajāpati.

23.3.28.a.m: And in the thousand-year [sessions], the Vaiśvasṛja fire-altar is obligatory.

23.3.29.a.s: abhiprayāyaṃ ced abhicinuyur uttaravedideśam etair mantrair abhimṛśet / yo 'sya supriyaḥ suvicita iva syāt tasmai vaiśvasṛjam / tṛtīye vā paryāye //
23.3.29.a.d: अभिप्रयायं चेद् अभिचिनुयुर् उत्तरवेदिदेशम् एतैर् मन्त्रैर् अभिमृशेत् । यो ऽस्य सुप्रियः सुविचित इव स्यात् तस्मै वैश्वसृजम् । तृतीये वा पर्याये ॥
23.3.29.a.m: If they pile it advancing forward, he should touch the place of the high altar with these mantras; he should pile the Vaiśvasṛja fire-altar for him who is very dear to him and well-chosen, as it were; or at the third turn.

23.3.30.a.m: Having combined the Sāvitra, Nāciketa, Cāturhotra, Vaiśvasṛja, and Āruṇaketuka fire-altars, they pile [them] even in a Soma sacrifice.

23.3.31.a.s: sāvitraḥ prathamā citiḥ / lokaṃpṛṇā dvitīyā / nāciketas tṛtīyā / lokaṃpṛṇā caturthī / cāturhotra uttamā [ pañcamī / vaiśvasṛjaḥ ṣaṣṭhī / āruṇaketukaḥ saptamī ] //
23.3.31.a.d: सावित्रः प्रथमा चितिः । लोकंपृणा द्वितीया । नाचिकेतस् तृतीया । लोकंपृणा चतुर्थी । चातुर्होत्र उत्तमा [ पञ्चमी । वैश्वसृजः षष्ठी । आरुणकेतुकः सप्तमी ] ॥
23.3.31.a.m: The Sāvitra is the first layer; the Lokampṛṇā is the second; the Nāciketa is the third; the Lokampṛṇā is the fourth; the Cāturhotra is the uppermost, [fifth; the Vaiśvasṛja is the sixth; the Āruṇaketuka is the seventh].

23.3.32.a.m: He draws a cup for Death from the broth of the animal victim offering.

23.3.33.a.s: etān agnīn [ pṛthak samāsena vā ] cinvāna ubhayīr dakṣiṇā dadāti kratudakṣiṇā [ yathāsamāmnātam ] agnidakṣināś ceti / kratudakṣiṇāḥ sarveṣām agnidakṣiṇāś cetur yadanuktaṃ mantrabrāhmaṇe tat prasiddham / [ atra pṛthag aprayujya na samasyante ] //
23.3.33.a.d: एतान् अग्नीन् [ पृथक् समासेन वा ] चिन्वान उभयीर् दक्षिणा ददाति क्रतुदक्षिणा [ यथासमाम्नातम् ] अग्निदक्षिनाश् चेति । क्रतुदक्षिणाः सर्वेषाम् अग्निदक्षिणाश् चेतुर् यदनुक्तं मन्त्रब्राह्मणे तत् प्रसिद्धम् । [ अत्र पृथग् अप्रयुज्य न समस्यन्ते ] ॥
23.3.33.a.m: Piling these fires [separately or collectively], he gives both sets of sacrificial fees: the fees for the sacrificial rite [as handed down in tradition] and the fees for the fire-altar. The fees for the sacrificial rite belong to all; and the fees for the fire-altar are known [from practice] where not stated in the mantra or brāhmaṇa; [here they are not combined without being employed separately].

23.3.34.a.s: [ agniṃ citvā sautrāmaṇyā yajeta / maitrāvaruṇyā vāmikṣayā ] //
23.3.34.a.d: [ अग्निं चित्वा सौत्रामण्या यजेत । मैत्रावरुण्या वामिक्षया ] ॥
23.3.34.a.m: [Having piled the fire-altar, he should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī, or with a curd-mixture for Mitra and Varuṇa].

23.3.35.a.m: The Āruṇaketuka fire-altar is explained by the Brāhmaṇa.

23.3.36.a.s: divaḥśyenībhir anvaham̐ svargakāmo yajeta / apādyābhiś ca / tā brāhmaṇavyākhyātāḥ //
23.3.36.a.d: दिवःश्येनीभिर् अन्वहम्̐ स्वर्गकामो यजेत । अपाद्याभिश् च । ता ब्राह्मणव्याख्याताः ॥
23.3.36.a.m: One desiring heaven should sacrifice daily with the Divaḥśyenī offerings and with the Apādyā offerings; they are explained by the Brāhmaṇa.

23.4.1.a.m: Now, of the unction rites, the Bṛhaspatisava has been explained.

23.4.2.a.s: vaiśyaḥ puṣṭikāma āgneyādīni sapta havīm̐ṣi nirvapati //
23.4.2.a.d: वैश्यः पुष्टिकाम आग्नेयादीनि सप्त हवीम्̐षि निर्वपति ॥
23.4.2.a.m: A vaiśya desiring prosperity pours out the seven oblations beginning with that to Agni.

23.4.3.a.s: pṛśniḥ paṣṭhauhī māruty ālabhyate tasyāḥ purastāt sviṣṭakṛto yajamānāyatana ṛṣabhacarma prācīnagrīvam uttaralomāstṛṇāti / tasminn āsīnaṃ dadhnābhiṣiñcati //
23.4.3.a.d: पृश्निः पष्ठौही मारुत्य् आलभ्यते तस्याः पुरस्तात् स्विष्टकृतो यजमानायतन ऋषभचर्म प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमास्तृणाति । तस्मिन्न् आसीनं दध्नाभिषिञ्चति ॥
23.4.3.a.m: A dappled four-year-old cow dedicated to the Maruts is immolated; prior to its Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he spreads out an ox-hide with its neck to the east and its hair upward in the sacrificer's seat; seated upon that, he consecrates him with curds.

23.4.4.a.s: brāhmaṇo brahmavarcasakāma āgneyādīny aṣṭau havīm̐ṣi nirvapati purastāt sviṣṭakṛto hiraṇyena ghṛtam utpūya tena kṛṣṇājina āsīnam abhiṣiñcati //
23.4.4.a.d: ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मवर्चसकाम आग्नेयादीन्य् अष्टौ हवीम्̐षि निर्वपति पुरस्तात् स्विष्टकृतो हिरण्येन घृतम् उत्पूय तेन कृष्णाजिन आसीनम् अभिषिञ्चति ॥
23.4.4.a.m: A brāhmaṇa desiring spiritual lustre pours out eight oblations beginning with that to Agni; prior to the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, having purified ghee with gold, he consecrates him seated on a black-antelope skin with that [ghee].

23.4.5.a.s: atha somasavaḥ / yat kiṃca rājasūyam ṛte somaṃ tat sarvaṃ bhavati //
23.4.5.a.d: अथ सोमसवः । यत् किंच राजसूयम् ऋते सोमं तत् सर्वं भवति ॥
23.4.5.a.m: Now the Somasava: whatever pertains to the Rājasūya, except for Soma, all that takes place.

23.4.6.a.m: Having concluded the offering to Mitra and Bṛhaspati, he immolates a barren cow dedicated to Soma.

23.4.7.a.s: tasyāḥ purastāt sviṣṭakṛtas \\ aṣāḍhaṃ yutsu pṛtanāsu paprim iti saumyarcādbhir abhiṣiñcati //
23.4.7.a.d: तस्याः पुरस्तात् स्विष्टकृतस् \\ अषाढं युत्सु पृतनासु पप्रिम् इति सौम्यर्चाद्भिर् अभिषिञ्चति ॥
23.4.7.a.m: Prior to its Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he consecrates him with water with the verse to Soma: 'Unconquered in battles, prevailing in combats...'

23.4.8.a.s: śeṣaṃ sam̐sthāpya sam̐sṛpām̐ havir diśām aveṣṭyā dvipaśunā paśubandhena sātyadūtānāṃ havirbhiḥ prayujām iti yajeta //
23.4.8.a.d: शेषं सम्̐स्थाप्य सम्̐सृपाम्̐ हविर् दिशाम् अवेष्ट्या द्विपशुना पशुबन्धेन सात्यदूतानां हविर्भिः प्रयुजाम् इति यजेत ॥
23.4.8.a.m: Having concluded the remainder, he should sacrifice with the oblations of the Saṃsṛps, with the Aveṣṭi of the quarters, with an animal sacrifice of two victims, and with the oblations of the Sātyadūtas, [saying,] 'May I enter into the Prayujs.'

23.4.9.a.s: pṛthisavena paśukāmaḥ / yat kiṃca rājasūyam anuttaravedikaṃ tat sarvaṃ bhavati //
23.4.9.a.d: पृथिसवेन पशुकामः । यत् किंच राजसूयम् अनुत्तरवेदिकं तत् सर्वं भवति ॥
23.4.9.a.m: One desiring cattle [should sacrifice] with the Pṛthisava; whatever pertains to the Rājasūya without a high altar, all that takes place.

23.4.10.a.s: maitrābārhaspatyasya purastāt sviṣṭakṛtas \\ ye me pañcāśatam iti nārāśam̐syarcādbhir abhiṣiñcati //
23.4.10.a.d: मैत्राबार्हस्पत्यस्य पुरस्तात् स्विष्टकृतस् \\ ये मे पञ्चाशतम् इति नाराशम्̐स्यर्चाद्भिर् अभिषिञ्चति ॥
23.4.10.a.m: Prior to the Sviṣṭakṛt offering of the oblation to Mitra and Bṛhaspati, he consecrates him with water with the Nārāśaṃsī verse: 'Those who fifty to me...'

23.4.11.a.m: The rest is identical with the preceding, except for the animal sacrifice.

23.4.13.a.m: One desiring food and nourishment should sacrifice with the Odanasava under the constellation Rohiṇī.

23.4.16.a.s: udita āditye sim̐he vyāghre \\ iti catasra āhutīr odanād dhutvā //
23.4.16.a.d: उदित आदित्ये सिम्̐हे व्याघ्रे \\ इति चतस्र आहुतीर् ओदनाद् धुत्वा ॥
23.4.16.a.m: When the sun has risen, having offered four oblations from the boiled rice with [the mantras beginning] 'In the lion, in the tiger...'

23.4.17.a.s: rāḍ asi \ virāḍ asi \\ ity etaiḥ pratimantraṃ manthān kalpayanti / ājyamanthaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ payomanthaṃ rājanyo dadhimanthaṃ vaiśya udamanthaṃ śūdraḥ
23.4.17.a.d: राड् असि \ विराड् असि \\ इत्य् एतैः प्रतिमन्त्रं मन्थान् कल्पयन्ति । आज्यमन्थं ब्राह्मणः पयोमन्थं राजन्यो दधिमन्थं वैश्य उदमन्थं शूद्रः
23.4.17.a.m: With these mantras, 'You are the ruler,' 'You are the wide ruler,' mantra by mantra, they prepare the barley-mash potions: a brāhmaṇa [prepares] the clarified butter mash, a rājanya the milk mash, a vaiśya the curds mash, and a śūdra the water mash.

23.4.18.a.s: indrāya tvā tejasvate tejasvantam̐ śrīṇāmi \\ iti / brāhmaṇaḥ saktubhir ājyam̐ śrītvā tejo 'si \\ ity abhimantrya tat te prayacchāmi \\ iti yajamānāya prayacchati //
23.4.18.a.d: इन्द्राय त्वा तेजस्वते तेजस्वन्तम्̐ श्रीणामि \\ इति । ब्राह्मणः सक्तुभिर् आज्यम्̐ श्रीत्वा तेजो ऽसि \\ इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य तत् ते प्रयच्छामि \\ इति यजमानाय प्रयच्छति ॥
23.4.18.a.m: With the mantra, 'For fiery Indra, I mix you full of fiery energy,' the brāhmaṇa, having mixed the clarified butter with barley-meal, touches it while reciting, 'You are fiery energy,' and gives it to the sacrificer, saying, 'That I offer to you.'

23.4.19.a.s: tejasvad astu me mukham iti pratigṛhya bhakṣayati
23.4.19.a.d: तेजस्वद् अस्तु मे मुखम् इति प्रतिगृह्य भक्षयति
23.4.19.a.m: Saying, 'May my mouth be full of fiery energy,' having received it, he eats it.

23.4.20.a.s: evam itareṣām uttarottaraśrayaṇo 'bhimantraṇaḥ pradāno bhakṣaṇaś ca yathāliṅgam
23.4.20.a.d: एवम् इतरेषाम् उत्तरोत्तरश्रयणो ऽभिमन्त्रणः प्रदानो भक्षणश् च यथालिङ्गम्
23.4.20.a.m: In the same manner for the others, the mixing, touching while reciting, offering, and eating follow in succession according to the characteristic mark [in the mantra].

23.4.21.a.s: sarvān yajamāno bhakṣayitvā hiraṇyaṃ brāhmaṇāya dadāti / tisṛdhanvam̐ rājanyāya / aṣṭrāṃ vaiśyāya / māṣakamaṇḍaluṃ śūdrāya
23.4.21.a.d: सर्वान् यजमानो भक्षयित्वा हिरण्यं ब्राह्मणाय ददाति । तिसृधन्वम्̐ राजन्याय । अष्ट्रां वैश्याय । माषकमण्डलुं शूद्राय
23.4.21.a.m: Having eaten all of them, the sacrificer gives gold to the brāhmaṇa, a bow with three arrows to the rājanya, a goad to the vaiśya, and a water-pot with black beans to the śūdra.

23.4.22.a.s: hiraṇyaṃ yajamānāyābadhnāti \\ āyur asi \ viśvāyur asi \\ ity ābadhyamāne japati //
23.4.22.a.d: हिरण्यं यजमानायाबध्नाति \\ आयुर् असि \ विश्वायुर् असि \\ इत्य् आबध्यमाने जपति ॥
23.4.22.a.m: He ties a piece of gold onto the sacrificer; while it is being tied on, he mutters: 'You are life, you are complete life...'

23.4.23.a.m: The sacrificer eats the remainder of the boiled rice.

23.4.24.a.s: imam agna āyuṣe varcase kṛdhi \\ iti prāśnantam abhimantrayate //
23.4.24.a.d: इमम् अग्न आयुषे वर्चसे कृधि \\ इति प्राश्नन्तम् अभिमन्त्रयते ॥
23.4.24.a.m: He recites over him as he eats: 'Make this man, O Agni, unto life, unto splendour...'

23.4.25.a.s: apāṃ grahān gṛhṇanti ye manthān kalpayanti \\ apāṃ yo dravaṇe rasas \\ ity etaiḥ pratimantram //
23.4.25.a.d: अपां ग्रहान् गृह्णन्ति ये मन्थान् कल्पयन्ति \\ अपां यो द्रवणे रसस् \\ इत्य् एतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
23.4.25.a.m: Those who prepare the barley-mash potions take water-cups, mantra by mantra, with these mantras: 'The sap which is in the running of the waters...'

23.4.26.a.s: tair enam̐ sam̐sṛṣṭair abhiṣiñcati \\ yato vāto manojavās \\ iti //
23.4.26.a.d: तैर् एनम्̐ सम्̐सृष्टैर् अभिषिञ्चति \\ यतो वातो मनोजवास् \\ इति ॥
23.4.26.a.m: With those [waters] commingled, he consecrates him, [saying,] 'Whence the wind, swift as thought...'

23.4.27.a.s: samudra ivāsi gahmanā \\ ity enam abhimantryāthainaṃ tribhir darbhapuñjīlaiḥ pavayati / avabhṛthapratyāmnāyo bhavatīti vijñāyate //
23.4.27.a.d: समुद्र इवासि गह्मना \\ इत्य् एनम् अभिमन्त्र्याथैनं त्रिभिर् दर्भपुञ्जीलैः पवयति । अवभृथप्रत्याम्नायो भवतीति विज्ञायते ॥
23.4.27.a.m: Having addressed him with 'You are like the sea in depth,' he then purifies him with three bunches of darbha-grass; it is taught: 'It serves as a substitute for the purificatory bath.'

23.4.28.a.m: A chariot stands positioned in front of the āhavanīya fire.

23.4.29.a.d: अभि प्रेहि \\ इति तं यजमानो ऽभ्येति
23.4.29.a.m: With the mantra, 'Go forward toward,' the sacrificer approaches it.

23.4.30.a.m: With the mantra, 'Mount, O strengthener of friends,' he recites over him as he mounts.

23.4.31.a.s: aṅkau nyaṅkau \\ iti rathacakre abhimṛśati / pakṣasī vā //
23.4.31.a.d: अङ्कौ न्यङ्कौ \\ इति रथचक्रे अभिमृशति । पक्षसी वा ॥
23.4.31.a.m: With the mantra, 'The hooks, the curved ones,' he touches the two chariot wheels, or the two sides [of the chariot].

23.4.32.a.m: With five [verses beginning] 'Mount, O slayer of Vṛtra,' [he recites over him when he has] mounted.

23.4.33.a.s: didṛkṣeṇyo darśanīyo bhavati / ya etena yajata iti vijñāyate
23.4.33.a.d: दिदृक्षेण्यो दर्शनीयो भवति । य एतेन यजत इति विज्ञायते
23.4.33.a.m: "He becomes worthy of being seen, handsome, who sacrifices with this," thus it is known [in the Brāhmaṇa].

23.4.37.a.s: tasya purorucaḥ / asyājarāsas \\ agna āyūm̐ṣi pavase \\ ity aindravāyavasya / dvitīyā maitrāvaruṇasya / tṛtīyāśvinasya / caturthī pañcamī ca śukrāmanthinoḥ ṣaṣṭhy āgrayaṇasya / anyām āgneyīm ukthyasya niyunakti / nityā dhruvasya / niyunakty aindrāgnavaiśvadevayoḥ / agniśriyas \\ iti tisro marutvatīyānām / śrudhi śrutkarṇa \\ ity uttarā māhendrasya / viśveṣām aditir iti tisra ādityagrahasya / uttamā sāvitrasya //
23.4.37.a.d: तस्य पुरोरुचः । अस्याजरासस् \\ अग्न आयूम्̐षि पवसे \\ इत्य् ऐन्द्रवायवस्य । द्वितीया मैत्रावरुणस्य । तृतीयाश्विनस्य । चतुर्थी पञ्चमी च शुक्रामन्थिनोः षष्ठ्य् आग्रयणस्य । अन्याम् आग्नेयीम् उक्थ्यस्य नियुनक्ति । नित्या ध्रुवस्य । नियुनक्त्य् ऐन्द्राग्नवैश्वदेवयोः । अग्निश्रियस् \\ इति तिस्रो मरुत्वतीयानाम् । श्रुधि श्रुत्कर्ण \\ इत्य् उत्तरा माहेन्द्रस्य । विश्वेषाम् अदितिर् इति तिस्र आदित्यग्रहस्य । उत्तमा सावित्रस्य ॥
23.4.37.a.m: Its introductory verses (puroruc): with "asyājarāsas" [and] "agna āyūṃṣi pavase" for the Aindravāyava graha; the second for the Maitrāvaruṇa; the third for the Āśvina; the fourth and fifth for the Śukra and Manthin; the sixth for the Āgrayaṇa; he assigns another verse to Agni for the Ukthya; the usual one for the Dhruva; he assigns [verses] for the Aindrāgna and Vaiśvadeva; "agniśriyas"—these three for the Marutvatīya cups; the next, "śrudhi śrutkarṇa", for the Māhendra; "viśveṣām aditir"—these three for the Āditya graha; the last for the Sāvitra;

23.4.38.a.s: niyunakti vaiśvadevasya / nityā pātnīvatasya / niyunakti hāriyojanasya //
23.4.38.a.d: नियुनक्ति वैश्वदेवस्य । नित्या पात्नीवतस्य । नियुनक्ति हारियोजनस्य ॥
23.4.38.a.m: he assigns [a verse] for the Vaiśvadeva; the usual one for the Pātnīvata; he assigns [a verse] for the Hāriyojana.

23.4.39.a.s: indrastutendrastomenokthyenendriyakāmo vīryakāmo vā yajeta / aindriyaḥ purorucas tiṣṭhā harī \ kasya vṛṣā \\ ity aindravāyavasya / tṛtīyā maitrāvaruṇasya / caturthy āśvinasya / pañcamī ṣaṣṭhī ca śukrāmanthinoḥ / saptamy āgrayaṇasya / nityokthyasya / niyunakti dhruvaindrāgnavaiśvadevānām / nityā marutvatīyamāhendrāṇām / ā no viśvābhir ūtibhir iti tisra ādityagrahasya / uttamā sāvitrasya //
23.4.39.a.d: इन्द्रस्तुतेन्द्रस्तोमेनोक्थ्येनेन्द्रियकामो वीर्यकामो वा यजेत । ऐन्द्रियः पुरोरुचस् तिष्ठा हरी \ कस्य वृषा \\ इत्य् ऐन्द्रवायवस्य । तृतीया मैत्रावरुणस्य । चतुर्थ्य् आश्विनस्य । पञ्चमी षष्ठी च शुक्रामन्थिनोः । सप्तम्य् आग्रयणस्य । नित्योक्थ्यस्य । नियुनक्ति ध्रुवैन्द्राग्नवैश्वदेवानाम् । नित्या मरुत्वतीयमाहेन्द्राणाम् । आ नो विश्वाभिर् ऊतिभिर् इति तिस्र आदित्यग्रहस्य । उत्तमा सावित्रस्य ॥
23.4.39.a.m: One who desires sensory power or desires heroic vigour should sacrifice with the Indrastut as an Indrastoma Ukthya. The introductory verses belong to Indra: with "tiṣṭhā harī" [and] "kasya vṛṣā" for the Aindravāyava graha; the third for the Maitrāvaruṇa; the fourth for the Āśvina; the fifth and sixth for the Śukra and Manthin; the seventh for the Āgrayaṇa; the usual one for the Ukthya; he assigns [verses] for the Dhruva, Aindrāgna, and Vaiśvadeva; the usual ones for the Marutvatīya and Māhendra cups; "ā no viśvābhir ūtibhir"—these three for the Āditya graha; the last for the Sāvitra;

23.4.40.a.d: नियुनक्ति वैश्वदेवपात्नीवतयोः । नित्या हारियोजनस्य । व्याख्यातो ऽप्तोर्यामः ॥
23.4.40.a.m: he assigns [verses] for the Vaiśvadeva and Pātnīvata; the usual one for the Hāriyojana. The Aptoryāma has been explained.

23.4.41.a.s: rājābhiṣekṣyamāṇo janapadeṣu samaveteṣu dvayoḥ puṇyāhayoḥ pūrvasmin sthaṇḍilaṃ kalpayitvāgnim upasamādhāya saṃparistīrya vasati //
23.4.41.a.d: राजाभिषेक्ष्यमाणो जनपदेषु समवेतेषु द्वयोः पुण्याहयोः पूर्वस्मिन् स्थण्डिलं कल्पयित्वाग्निम् उपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य वसति ॥
23.4.41.a.m: A king about to be consecrated, when the people of the country have assembled, on the earlier of two auspicious days, having prepared a mound, having placed the fire upon it, and having strewn [grass] around it, stays [the night].

23.4.42.a.s: udita āditye ye keśinas \\ narte brahmaṇas \\ iti dve āhutī hutvā rāḍ asi \ virāḍ asi \\ iti yajamānāyatana audumbarīm āsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati //
23.4.42.a.d: उदित आदित्ये ये केशिनस् \\ नर्ते ब्रह्मणस् \\ इति द्वे आहुती हुत्वा राड् असि \ विराड् असि \\ इति यजमानायतन औदुम्बरीम् आसन्दीं प्रतिष्ठापयति ॥
23.4.42.a.m: When the sun has risen, having offered two oblations with "ye keśinas" and "narte brahmaṇas", he sets up an udumbara throne in the sacrificer's place with "rāḍ asi" [and] "virāḍ asi".

23.4.44.a.m: He addresses him as he mounts with "āroha proṣṭham".

23.4.46.a.s: tasyām āsīnaḥ keśān vāpayate yenāvapat savitā kṣureṇa \\ iti //
23.4.46.a.d: तस्याम् आसीनः केशान् वापयते येनावपत् सविता क्षुरेण \\ इति ॥
23.4.46.a.m: Seated on it, he has his hair shaved with "yenāvapat savitā kṣureṇa".

23.4.47.a.s: mā te keśān iti keśān prakīryamāṇān anumantrayate
23.4.47.a.d: मा ते केशान् इति केशान् प्रकीर्यमाणान् अनुमन्त्रयते
23.4.47.a.m: With "mā te keśān" he recites over the falling hair.

23.4.48.a.s: tān samopya darbhastambe nidadhāti tebhyo nidhānam iti //
23.4.48.a.d: तान् समोप्य दर्भस्तम्बे निदधाति तेभ्यो निधानम् इति ॥
23.4.48.a.m: Having collected it, he deposits it in a clump of darbha grass with "tebhyo nidhānam".

23.4.49.a.s: athainam ājyamiśreṇa payasānakti / balaṃ te bāhuvor iti bāhū / yat sīmantam iti śiraḥ / vyāghro 'yam agnau \\ iti saptāhutīr hutvā dyaur asi \ pṛthivy asi \\ iti yajamānāyatane śārdūlacarma prācīnagrīvam uttaralomāstṛṇāti / tasmin rājopaviśati //
23.4.49.a.d: अथैनम् आज्यमिश्रेण पयसानक्ति । बलं ते बाहुवोर् इति बाहू । यत् सीमन्तम् इति शिरः । व्याघ्रो ऽयम् अग्नौ \\ इति सप्ताहुतीर् हुत्वा द्यौर् असि \ पृथिव्य् असि \\ इति यजमानायतने शार्दूलचर्म प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमास्तृणाति । तस्मिन् राजोपविशति ॥
23.4.49.a.m: Then he anoints him with milk mixed with clarified butter: the arms with "balaṃ te bāhuvor", the head with "yat sīmantam". Having offered seven oblations with "vyāghro 'yam agnau", he spreads out a tiger skin with the neck to the east and the hair side up in the sacrificer's place with "dyaur asi" [and] "pṛthivy asi". The king sits upon it.

23.4.50.a.m: He addresses him as he is seated with "vyāghro vaiyāghre".

23.4.51.a.s: athainaṃ tokmāvāstābhir dūrvāvāstābhir vādbhir abhiṣiñcati yā divyā āpas \\ iti pratipadyā pāṅktāt //
23.4.51.a.d: अथैनं तोक्मावास्ताभिर् दूर्वावास्ताभिर् वाद्भिर् अभिषिञ्चति या दिव्या आपस् \\ इति प्रतिपद्या पाङ्क्तात् ॥
23.4.51.a.m: Then he consecrates him with waters containing young barley sprouts or waters containing dūrvā grass, beginning with "yā divyā āpas" up to the end of the paṅkti stanza.

23.4.52.a.s: aruṇaṃ tvā vṛkam ity enam abhimantrya //
23.4.52.a.d: अरुणं त्वा वृकम् इत्य् एनम् अभिमन्त्र्य ॥
23.4.52.a.m: Having addressed him with "aruṇaṃ tvā vṛkam",

23.4.53.a.m: having stretched out his arms with "pra bāhavā",

23.4.54.a.m: he lowers them with "indrasya te vīryakṛtas".

23.4.55.a.s: agreṇāgnim̐ ratho 'vasthito bhavati / abhi prehi \\ iti taṃ rājābhyeti //
23.4.55.a.d: अग्रेणाग्निम्̐ रथो ऽवस्थितो भवति । अभि प्रेहि \\ इति तं राजाभ्येति ॥
23.4.55.a.m: A chariot stands in front of the fire; the king approaches it with "abhi prehi".

23.4.56.a.m: He addresses him as he mounts with "ātiṣṭha vṛtrahantamas".

23.4.57.a.s: aṅkau nyaṅkau \\ iti rathacakre abhimṛśati / pakṣasī vā //
23.4.57.a.d: अङ्कौ न्यङ्कौ \\ इति रथचक्रे अभिमृशति । पक्षसी वा ॥
23.4.57.a.m: With "aṅkau nyaṅkau" he touches the two chariot wheels, or the two side-rails.

23.4.58.a.s: namas ta ṛṣe \\ iti purohitam abhimantrayate //
23.4.58.a.d: नमस् त ऋषे \\ इति पुरोहितम् अभिमन्त्रयते ॥
23.4.58.a.m: With "namas ta ṛṣe" he addresses the royal chaplain (purohita).

23.4.60.a.m: With "ā raśmīn" he takes hold of the reins.

23.4.61.a.m: With the six verses [beginning with] "ātiṣṭha vṛtrahan" [he addresses] him when he has mounted.

23.4.62.a.s: pari mā senyās \\ iti dve vācayitvā //
23.4.62.a.d: परि मा सेन्यास् \\ इति द्वे वाचयित्वा ॥
23.4.62.a.m: Having made him recite the two [verses] beginning with "pari mā senyās",

23.4.63.a.m: having addressed [him] with the subsequent three [verses],

23.4.64.a.s: ud asāv etu \\ ity ādityam udīkṣayati //
23.4.64.a.d: उद् असाव् एतु \\ इत्य् आदित्यम् उदीक्षयति ॥
23.4.64.a.m: he makes him look up at the sun with "ud asāv etu".

23.4.65.a.m: With "annavatām" [the king] looks out over the people of the realm.

24.1.1.a.s: pravargyaṃ saṃbhariṣyann amāvāsyāyaṃ paurṇamāsyām āpūryamāṇapakṣe vā puṇye nakṣatre tūṣṇīṃ kāṇṭakīṃ samidham ādhāya yuñjate manas \\ iti caturgṛhītaṃ juhoti //
24.1.1.a.d: प्रवर्ग्यं संभरिष्यन्न् अमावास्यायं पौर्णमास्याम् आपूर्यमाणपक्षे वा पुण्ये नक्षत्रे तूष्णीं काण्टकीं समिधम् आधाय युञ्जते मनस् \\ इति चतुर्गृहीतं जुहोति ॥
24.1.1.a.m: Intending to collect the materials for the Pravargya, on the New Moon or Full Moon day, or in the waxing half of the month under an auspicious lunar mansion, having silently placed a thorny piece of firewood [on the fire], he offers four ladlefuls [of clarified butter] with "yuñjate manas".

24.1.2.a.s: na dīkṣitasya juhuyāt kāṇṭakīm evaitayā samidham ādadhyād yajur eva vā vaded ity eke //
24.1.2.a.d: न दीक्षितस्य जुहुयात् काण्टकीम् एवैतया समिधम् आदध्याद् यजुर् एव वा वदेद् इत्य् एके ॥
24.1.2.a.m: For an already initiated sacrificer he should not offer; he should only place a thorny piece of firewood with this [mantra], or he should merely recite the yajus, say some [authorities].

24.1.3.a.s: devasya tvā \\ ity abhrim ādatte khādirīm audumbarīṃ vaiṇavīṃ vaikaṅkatīṃ vā pūrvavat pramāṇām abhrir asi \ nārir asi \\ ity abhimantrayate //
24.1.3.a.d: देवस्य त्वा \\ इत्य् अभ्रिम् आदत्ते खादिरीम् औदुम्बरीं वैणवीं वैकङ्कतीं वा पूर्ववत् प्रमाणाम् अभ्रिर् असि \ नारिर् असि \\ इत्य् अभिमन्त्रयते ॥
24.1.3.a.m: With "devasya tvā" he takes up a spade of khadira, udumbara, bamboo, or vikankata wood, of the previously prescribed measure; he addresses it with "abhrir asi" [and] "nārir asi".

24.1.4.a.s: uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate \\ iti brahmāṇam āmantrayate / upottiṣṭhati brahmobhāv uttaram ardharcaṃ japataḥ //
24.1.4.a.d: उत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पते \\ इति ब्रह्माणम् आमन्त्रयते । उपोत्तिष्ठति ब्रह्मोभाव् उत्तरम् अर्धर्चं जपतः ॥
24.1.4.a.m: With "uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate" he calls upon the brahman; the brahman stands up; both mutter the subsequent half-verse.

24.1.5.a.s: praitu brahmaṇaspatir iti prāñco 'śvaprathamā gacchanti yatra saṃbhārān vechyanto gacchanti purastād evāsyaite pariśrite 'bhyudāhṛtā bhavantīti vijñāyate //
24.1.5.a.d: प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिर् इति प्राञ्चो ऽश्वप्रथमा गच्छन्ति यत्र संभारान् वेछ्यन्तो गच्छन्ति पुरस्ताद् एवास्यैते परिश्रिते ऽभ्युदाहृता भवन्तीति विज्ञायते ॥
24.1.5.a.m: With "praitu brahmaṇaspatir" they proceed eastward led by a horse, going where they will search for the materials; "these [materials] have indeed already been brought near beforehand inside the enclosure," thus it is known [in the Brāhmaṇa].

24.1.6.a.s: agreṇāhavanīyaṃ mṛtkhanaḥ pūrvaḥpūrva itara uttareṇa mṛtkhanaṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomāstīrya devī dyāvāpṛthivī iti dyāvāpṛthivī abhimantrayate mṛtkhanaṃ vā \\ ṛdhyāsam iti mṛtkhane 'bhriyā praharati makhasya śiras \\ ity apādāya makhāya tvā \\ iti harati makhasya tvā śīrṣṇe \\ iti kṛṣṇājine nivapati //
24.1.6.a.d: अग्रेणाहवनीयं मृत्खनः पूर्वःपूर्व इतर उत्तरेण मृत्खनं कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमास्तीर्य देवी द्यावापृथिवी इति द्यावापृथिवी अभिमन्त्रयते मृत्खनं वा \\ ऋध्यासम् इति मृत्खने ऽभ्रिया प्रहरति मखस्य शिरस् \\ इत्य् अपादाय मखाय त्वा \\ इति हरति मखस्य त्वा शीर्ष्णे \\ इति कृष्णाजिने निवपति ॥
24.1.6.a.m: East of the āhavanīya fire is a clay pit; the one [pit] is to the east, the other [further] east; having spread out a black antelope skin to the north of the clay pit with the neck to the east and the hair side up, he addresses heaven and earth, or the clay pit, with "devī dyāvāpṛthivī"; with "ṛdhyāsam" he strikes into the clay pit with the spade; having dug it out with "makhasya śiras", he carries it with "makhāya tvā"; he pours it onto the black antelope skin with "makhasya tvā śīrṣṇe".

24.1.7.a.s: evaṃ dvitīyaṃ ca tṛtīyaṃ ca harati //
24.1.7.a.d: एवं द्वितीयं च तृतीयं च हरति ॥
24.1.7.a.m: In the same manner he carries [clay] a second and a third time.

24.1.8.a.s: tūṣṇīṃ caturthaṃ yāvatīṃ mṛdaṃ pravargyapātrebhya āptāṃ manyate //
24.1.8.a.d: तूष्णीं चतुर्थं यावतीं मृदं प्रवर्ग्यपात्रेभ्य आप्तां मन्यते ॥
24.1.8.a.m: Silently a fourth time, as much clay as he considers sufficient for the Pravargya vessels.

24.1.10.a.s: iyaty agra āsīr iti varāhavihatam abhimantrayate devīr vamrīr iti valmīkavapām indrasyaujo 'si \\ iti pūtikān agnijā asi prajāpate retas \\ iti kṛṣṇājinalomāny ajalomāni ca sam̐sṛṣṭāni saṃbhṛtya \\ āyur dhehi \ prāṇaṃ dhehi \\ ity etair aśvenāvaghrāpya madhu tvā madhulā karotu \\ ity ajayā puṃchagalayābhidogdhi //
24.1.10.a.d: इयत्य् अग्र आसीर् इति वराहविहतम् अभिमन्त्रयते देवीर् वम्रीर् इति वल्मीकवपाम् इन्द्रस्यौजो ऽसि \\ इति पूतिकान् अग्निजा असि प्रजापते रेतस् \\ इति कृष्णाजिनलोमान्य् अजलोमानि च सम्̐सृष्टानि संभृत्य \\ आयुर् धेहि \ प्राणं धेहि \\ इत्य् एतैर् अश्वेनावघ्राप्य मधु त्वा मधुला करोतु \\ इत्य् अजया पुंछगलयाभिदोग्धि ॥
24.1.10.a.m: With "iyaty agra āsīr" he addresses [earth] thrown up by a boar; with "devīr vamrīr" an anthill mound; with "indrasyaujo 'si" the pūtīka plants; with "agnijā asi prajāpate retas", having gathered mixed hairs of a black antelope and hairs of a goat; having made the horse sniff [the materials] with "āyur dhehi" [and] "prāṇaṃ dhehi", he milks over them [milk from] a she-goat that has borne a male kid, with "madhu tvā madhulā karotu".

24.1.11.a.m: Some teach that the milking over [the materials] comes earlier.

24.1.12.a.s: bahava āryāḥ parigṛhya haranty uttareṇa vihāraṃ pariśrita uddhate 'vokṣite sikatopāpte nidadhati //
24.1.12.a.d: बहव आर्याः परिगृह्य हरन्त्य् उत्तरेण विहारं परिश्रित उद्धते ऽवोक्षिते सिकतोपाप्ते निदधति ॥
24.1.12.a.m: Many Āryas, taking hold of [the materials], carry them; north of the sacrificial area, within the enclosure, on a raised, sprinkled, sand-covered place, they set them down.

24.1.13.a.s: madhu tvā madhulā karotu \\ iti madantīr upasṛjyaitair evokhāsam̐sarjanaiḥ sam̐sṛjati yat kiṃca pravargya udakakṛtyaṃ madantībhir eva tat kriyata ity atyantapradeśo nainam̐ strī prekṣate na śūdro na kurvann abhiprāṇity apahāya mukham anabhiprāṇan veṇunā karoti //
24.1.13.a.d: मधु त्वा मधुला करोतु \\ इति मदन्तीर् उपसृज्यैतैर् एवोखासम्̐सर्जनैः सम्̐सृजति यत् किंच प्रवर्ग्य उदककृत्यं मदन्तीभिर् एव तत् क्रियत इत्य् अत्यन्तप्रदेशो नैनम्̐ स्त्री प्रेक्षते न शूद्रो न कुर्वन्न् अभिप्राणित्य् अपहाय मुखम् अनभिप्राणन् वेणुना करोति ॥
24.1.13.a.m: With "madhu tvā madhulā karotu", having poured in boiled water, he mixes [the clay] with these very formulas for mixing the ukhā pot; "whatever water-rite is in the Pravargya is done with boiled water only," such is the absolute rule; no woman looks at it, nor a Śūdra; while doing it he does not breathe upon it; turning his face away and holding his breath, he works it with a bamboo stick.

24.1.14.a.s: na pravargyam ādityaṃ ca vyaveyād yatra kvaca viprakrānte pravargya ādityo 'stam iyāt kṛtāntād eva viramec chvo bhūte śeṣaṃ samāpnuyāt //
24.1.14.a.d: न प्रवर्ग्यम् आदित्यं च व्यवेयाद् यत्र क्वच विप्रक्रान्ते प्रवर्ग्य आदित्यो ऽस्तम् इयात् कृतान्ताद् एव विरमेच् छ्वो भूते शेषं समाप्नुयात् ॥
24.1.14.a.m: One should not step between the pravargya and the sun. Wherever the sun might set while the pravargya is underway, he should stop only at the end of a completed rite; when the next day comes, he should complete the remainder.

24.1.15.a.s: saṃplonmāya mṛdam \\ makhasya śiro 'si \\ iti piṇḍaṃ karoti yajñasya pade sthas \\ ity aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ nigṛhya gāyatreṇa tvā chandasā karomi \\ iti tribhiś chandobhir mahāvīraṃ karoti vāyavyaprakāraṃ tryuddhiṃ pañcoddhim aparimitoddhiṃ vā //
24.1.15.a.d: संप्लोन्माय मृदम् \\ मखस्य शिरो ऽसि \\ इति पिण्डं करोति यज्ञस्य पदे स्थस् \\ इत्य् अङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां निगृह्य गायत्रेण त्वा छन्दसा करोमि \\ इति त्रिभिश् छन्दोभिर् महावीरं करोति वायव्यप्रकारं त्र्युद्धिं पञ्चोद्धिम् अपरिमितोद्धिं वा ॥
24.1.15.a.m: Having sprinkled and measured out the clay, he forms a lump with, 'You are the head of Makha.' Having gripped it with his two thumbs with, 'You two are the feet of the sacrifice,' he makes the mahāvīra pot with the three metres, with 'I make you with the gāyatrī metre,' in the shape of a vāyavya cup, with three elevations, with five elevations, or with an unmeasured number of elevations.

24.1.16.a.s: makhasya rāsnāsi \\ iti madhyadeśa upabilaṃ rāsnāṃ karoty aditis te bilaṃ gṛhṇātu \\ iti veṇuparvaṇā bilaṃ karoti yāvad daivatāya sauviṣṭakṛtāyāgnihotrāya bhakṣāyāptaṃ manyate //
24.1.16.a.d: मखस्य रास्नासि \\ इति मध्यदेश उपबिलं रास्नां करोत्य् अदितिस् ते बिलं गृह्णातु \\ इति वेणुपर्वणा बिलं करोति यावद् दैवताय सौविष्टकृतायाग्निहोत्राय भक्षायाप्तं मन्यते ॥
24.1.16.a.m: With, 'You are the girdle of Makha,' he makes a girdle in the middle part near the opening. With, 'May Aditi take hold of your opening,' he makes the opening with a bamboo joint, as much as he thinks sufficient for the divinity, for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, for the Agnihotra, and for the portion to be consumed.

24.1.17.a.s: sūryasya harasā śrāya \\ ity uttarataḥ sikatāsu pratiṣṭhāpya makho 'si \\ ity abhimantrayate makhāya tvā \\ iti vaivam itarāv api vā gāyatreṇa \\ iti prathamaṃ traiṣṭubhena \\ iti dvitīyaṃ jāgatena \\ iti tṛtīyaṃ tūṣṇīm itarāṇi //
24.1.17.a.d: सूर्यस्य हरसा श्राय \\ इत्य् उत्तरतः सिकतासु प्रतिष्ठाप्य मखो ऽसि \\ इत्य् अभिमन्त्रयते मखाय त्वा \\ इति वैवम् इतराव् अपि वा गायत्रेण \\ इति प्रथमं त्रैष्टुभेन \\ इति द्वितीयं जागतेन \\ इति तृतीयं तूष्णीम् इतराणि ॥
24.1.17.a.m: Having placed it firmly on the sand to the north with, 'Be heated by the heat of Sūrya,' he consecrates it with, 'You are Makha,' or with, 'For Makha, you.' In this manner [he makes] the other two as well; or rather, the first with the gāyatrī metre, the second with the triṣṭubh metre, the third with the jagatī metre, and the other [implements] silently.

24.1.18.a.s: etasyā eva mṛdo dogdhre yathā srug adaṇḍaivam̐ hastyoṣṭhye varṣīya ādhvaryavam̐ hrasīyaḥ pratiprasthānam ājyasthālīm̐ rauhiṇyakapale ca parimaṇḍale gharmeṣṭakāṃ kulāyinīṃ ca yadi sāgnicityo bhavati //
24.1.18.a.d: एतस्या एव मृदो दोग्ध्रे यथा स्रुग् अदण्डैवम्̐ हस्त्योष्ठ्ये वर्षीय आध्वर्यवम्̐ ह्रसीयः प्रतिप्रस्थानम् आज्यस्थालीम्̐ रौहिण्यकपले च परिमण्डले घर्मेष्टकां कुलायिनीं च यदि साग्निचित्यो भवति ॥
24.1.18.a.m: From this very clay [he makes] two milking vessels, like a ladle without a handle, with a snout like an elephant's trunk—the adhvaryu's larger, the pratiprasthātṛ's smaller; an ājya pot, two circular potsherds for the rauhiṇa cakes, and, if [the sacrifice] is accompanied by the construction of the fire altar, the gharmestakā and kulāyinī bricks.

24.1.19.a.s: gārhapatye 'śvaśakṛnty upasamādhāya vṛṣṇe aśvasya niṣpad asi \\ iti prathamakṛtaṃ mahāvīraṃ śaphābhyāṃ parigṛhya dhūpayaty evam itarau tūṣṇīm itarāṇi śaphābhyām evāta ūrdhvaṃ mahāvīrān ādatte //
24.1.19.a.d: गार्हपत्ये ऽश्वशकृन्त्य् उपसमाधाय वृष्णे अश्वस्य निष्पद् असि \\ इति प्रथमकृतं महावीरं शफाभ्यां परिगृह्य धूपयत्य् एवम् इतरौ तूष्णीम् इतराणि शफाभ्याम् एवात ऊर्ध्वं महावीरान् आदत्ते ॥
24.1.19.a.m: Having added horse dung to the gārhapatya fire, he fumigates the first-made mahāvīra pot, gripping it with the two pincers, with, 'For the stallion you are the horse's dung.' In this manner [he treats] the other two, and the other [objects] silently. From this point forward he grasps the mahāvīra pots only with the two pincers.

24.1.20.a.s: agreṇa gārhapatyam avaṭaṃ khātvā lohitapacanīyaiḥ saṃbhārair avastīrya deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tvā \\ iti teṣu prathamakṛtaṃ mahāvīram upāvaharaty evam itarau tūṣṇīm itarāṇy anvavadhāya lohitapacanīyaiḥ saṃbhāraiḥ pracchādya gārhapatye muñjapralavān ādīpya \\ arciṣe tvā \ śociṣe tvā \\ ity etaiḥ pratimantraṃ pratidiśam upoṣati sarvaiḥ sarvataḥ //
24.1.20.a.d: अग्रेण गार्हपत्यम् अवटं खात्वा लोहितपचनीयैः संभारैर् अवस्तीर्य देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वा \\ इति तेषु प्रथमकृतं महावीरम् उपावहरत्य् एवम् इतरौ तूष्णीम् इतराण्य् अन्ववधाय लोहितपचनीयैः संभारैः प्रच्छाद्य गार्हपत्ये मुञ्जप्रलवान् आदीप्य \\ अर्चिषे त्वा \ शोचिषे त्वा \\ इत्य् एतैः प्रतिमन्त्रं प्रतिदिशम् उपोषति सर्वैः सर्वतः ॥
24.1.20.a.m: Having dug a pit in front of the gārhapatya fire and strewn it with materials for red-baking, he sets down the first-made mahāvīra pot into them with, 'O god who walks ahead, may I bear you.' In this manner [he sets down] the other two, puts down the other [objects] silently, covers them with materials for red-baking, ignites reed stalks in the gārhapatya fire, and burns around [the pit] in each direction, mantra by mantra, with, 'For the flame, you,' 'For the blaze, you,' and from all sides with all [mantras].

24.1.21.a.s: abhīmaṃ mahinā divam ity etābhyāṃ pacyamānāny upacarati pakveṣu siddhyai tvā \\ iti dhṛṣṭī ādāya devas tvā savitodvapatu \\ iti prathamakṛtaṃ mahāvīram udvāsya \\ apadyamānaḥ pṛthivyām \ āśā diśa āpṛṇa \\ ity uttarataḥ sikatāsu pratiṣṭhāpayaty evam itarau tūṣṇīm itarāṇy udvāsya //
24.1.21.a.d: अभीमं महिना दिवम् इत्य् एताभ्यां पच्यमानान्य् उपचरति पक्वेषु सिद्ध्यै त्वा \\ इति धृष्टी आदाय देवस् त्वा सवितोद्वपतु \\ इति प्रथमकृतं महावीरम् उद्वास्य \\ अपद्यमानः पृथिव्याम् \ आशा दिश आपृण \\ इत्य् उत्तरतः सिकतासु प्रतिष्ठापयत्य् एवम् इतरौ तूष्णीम् इतराण्य् उद्वास्य ॥
24.1.21.a.m: He attends upon them while they are baking with the two [mantras] beginning, 'Over this heaven with greatness.' When they are baked, having taken two fire sticks with, 'For success, you,' and having taken out the first-made mahāvīra pot with, 'May the divine Savitṛ take you out,' he sets it down firmly on the sand to the north with, 'Not falling upon the earth,' and, 'Fill the quarters, the intermediate quarters.' In this manner [he sets down] the other two, having taken out the other [objects] silently.

24.1.22.a.s: sūryasya tvā cakṣuṣānvīkṣe \\ ity anuvīkṣate \\ idam aham amum āmuṣyāyaṇaṃ viśā paśubhir brahmavarcasena paryūhāmi \\ iti triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ sikatābhiḥ paryūhati viśā \\ iti rājanyasya paśubhir iti vaiśyasya gāyatreṇa tvā chandasācchṛṇadmi \\ ity etair ajakṣīreṇācchṛṇatti tribhistribhir ekaikam̐ sarvair evaikaikaṃ tān kṛṣṇājina upanahya deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tvā \\ ity āsajaty upariṣṭātkāla eṣa mantro bhavatīti vijñāyate //
24.1.22.a.d: सूर्यस्य त्वा चक्षुषान्वीक्षे \\ इत्य् अनुवीक्षते \\ इदम् अहम् अमुम् आमुष्यायणं विशा पशुभिर् ब्रह्मवर्चसेन पर्यूहामि \\ इति त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं सिकताभिः पर्यूहति विशा \\ इति राजन्यस्य पशुभिर् इति वैश्यस्य गायत्रेण त्वा छन्दसाच्छृणद्मि \\ इत्य् एतैर् अजक्षीरेणाच्छृणत्ति त्रिभिस्त्रिभिर् एकैकम्̐ सर्वैर् एवैकैकं तान् कृष्णाजिन उपनह्य देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वा \\ इत्य् आसजत्य् उपरिष्टात्काल एष मन्त्रो भवतीति विज्ञायते ॥
24.1.22.a.m: He looks upon it with, 'I look upon you with the eye of the Sun.' With, 'Here I surround that son of that man with the peasantry, with cattle, with spiritual lustre,' he surrounds it three times from left to right with sand—'with the peasantry' for a rājanya, 'with cattle' for a vaiśya. With, 'I pierce you with the gāyatrī metre,' he sprinkles it with goat's milk using these [mantras]—each one with three [mantras], or each one with all [mantras]. Having tied them up in a black antelope skin, he hangs them up with, 'O god who walks ahead, may I bear you.' It is taught that this mantra belongs to the subsequent time.

24.2.1.a.s: pravargyeṇa pracariṣyantaḥ saṃvṛṇvanti dvārāṇi pariśrayanti patnyāḥ
24.2.1.a.d: प्रवर्ग्येण प्रचरिष्यन्तः संवृण्वन्ति द्वाराणि परिश्रयन्ति पत्न्याः
24.2.1.a.m: Being about to proceed with the pravargya, they close the doors and screen off the sacrificer's wife.

24.2.2.a.s: paścād dhotopaviśati purastād adhvaryur dakṣiṇato brahmā yajamānaś ca dakṣiṇataḥpaścāt prastotottarata āgnīdhraḥ pratiprasthātā ca //
24.2.2.a.d: पश्चाद् धोतोपविशति पुरस्ताद् अध्वर्युर् दक्षिणतो ब्रह्मा यजमानश् च दक्षिणतःपश्चात् प्रस्तोतोत्तरत आग्नीध्रः प्रतिप्रस्थाता च ॥
24.2.2.a.m: The hotṛ sits down in the west, the adhvaryu in the east, the brahman and the sacrificer in the south, the prastotṛ in the south-west, and the āgnīdhra and the pratiprasthātṛ in the north.

24.2.3.a.s: madantībhir upaspṛśya prathamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvottareṇa vihāraṃ muñjapralavān sam̐stīrya deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tvā \\ iti teṣu prathamakṛtaṃ mahāvīram upāvaharaty evam itarau tūṣṇīm itarāṇi //
24.2.3.a.d: मदन्तीभिर् उपस्पृश्य प्रथमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वोत्तरेण विहारं मुञ्जप्रलवान् सम्̐स्तीर्य देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वा \\ इति तेषु प्रथमकृतं महावीरम् उपावहरत्य् एवम् इतरौ तूष्णीम् इतराणि ॥
24.2.3.a.m: Having touched boiled water and performed the propitiatory rite with the first anuvāka, having strewn reed stalks to the north of the sacrificial area, he sets down the first-made mahāvīra pot onto them with, 'O god who walks ahead, may I bear you.' In this manner [he sets down] the other two, and the other [objects] silently.

24.2.4.a.s: atraiva sarvaṃ parigharmyaṃ saṃpādayaty audumbarāṇi vyākhyāsyāmaḥ samrāḍāsandīm agreṇa yathā rājāsandīṃ rājāsandīṃ varṣīyasīm eke samāmananti samrāḍāsandīm eke mauñjībhī rajjubhir ekasarābhir vyūtāṃ ca //
24.2.4.a.d: अत्रैव सर्वं परिघर्म्यं संपादयत्य् औदुम्बराणि व्याख्यास्यामः सम्राडासन्दीम् अग्रेण यथा राजासन्दीं राजासन्दीं वर्षीयसीम् एके समामनन्ति सम्राडासन्दीम् एके मौञ्जीभी रज्जुभिर् एकसराभिर् व्यूतां च ॥
24.2.4.a.m: Right here he prepares all the implements for the gharma. We shall describe those made of udumbara wood: the samrāj-seat in front, like the rājan-seat. Some teach that the rājan-seat is larger; some teach that the samrāj-seat is woven with single-strand cords of muñja grass.

24.2.5.a.s: catasraḥ srucas tāsāṃ dve aniṣṭabdhe te rauhiṇahavanyau niṣṭabdhayor varṣīyasy upayamanī prokṣaṇīdhānyanyā sruvau dhṛṣṭī śaphau mahāvīrasaṃmitāvraskau methī trīn mayūkhān ṣaṭ śakalām̐s trayodaśa vaikaṅkatān paridhīn kāṇṭakīṃ ca samidhaṃ vaiṇavāni gharmendhanāni khādirāṇi pālāśāny audumbarāṇy arkamayāni śamīmayāni vā //
24.2.5.a.d: चतस्रः स्रुचस् तासां द्वे अनिष्टब्धे ते रौहिणहवन्यौ निष्टब्धयोर् वर्षीयस्य् उपयमनी प्रोक्षणीधान्यन्या स्रुवौ धृष्टी शफौ महावीरसंमिताव्रस्कौ मेथी त्रीन् मयूखान् षट् शकलाम्̐स् त्रयोदश वैकङ्कतान् परिधीन् काण्टकीं च समिधं वैणवानि घर्मेन्धनानि खादिराणि पालाशान्य् औदुम्बराण्य् अर्कमयानि शमीमयानि वा ॥
24.2.5.a.m: There are four srucs: of these, two are without supporting pegs—those are the two offering ladles for the rauhiṇa cakes; of the two with pegs, the larger is the supporting ladle, the other is the sprinkling vessel; two dipping ladles, two fire sticks, two pincers with chips cut off to match the mahāvīra pot, a peg, three pins, six chips, thirteen vaikaṅkata enclosing sticks, a thorny stick of firewood, and fuel for the gharma made of bamboo, khadira, palāśa, udumbara, arka, or śamī wood.

24.2.6.a.s: trīṇi kārṣṇājināni dhavitrāṇi śuklakṛṣṇalomāni teṣāṃ vaiṇavā bāhumātrā daṇḍā bhavanty audumbarā vā rajatasuvarṇau rukmau pṛthakśatamānau mauñjāni vyākhyāsyāmo dvau vedau tayor anyataraḥ parivāsino 'bhidhānī nidāne catvāri viśākhadāmāni pralavām̐ś cāpraviśīrṇāgrān kharebhyaḥ sikatā rauhiṇayoḥ piṣṭāny aphalīkṛtānāṃ mauñje pavitre darbhamaye vā tūṣṇīm ājyaṃ prokṣaṇīś ca sam̐skṛtya //
24.2.6.a.d: त्रीणि कार्ष्णाजिनानि धवित्राणि शुक्लकृष्णलोमानि तेषां वैणवा बाहुमात्रा दण्डा भवन्त्य् औदुम्बरा वा रजतसुवर्णौ रुक्मौ पृथक्शतमानौ मौञ्जानि व्याख्यास्यामो द्वौ वेदौ तयोर् अन्यतरः परिवासिनो ऽभिधानी निदाने चत्वारि विशाखदामानि प्रलवाम्̐श् चाप्रविशीर्णाग्रान् खरेभ्यः सिकता रौहिणयोः पिष्टान्य् अफलीकृतानां मौञ्जे पवित्रे दर्भमये वा तूष्णीम् आज्यं प्रोक्षणीश् च सम्̐स्कृत्य ॥
24.2.6.a.m: There are three fans made of black antelope skin with white and black hair; their handles are made of bamboo, a cubit long, or of udumbara wood; two gold and silver plates, each weighing a hundred mānas. We shall describe the items made of muñja grass: two vedas, one of which is trimmed; a halter, two tie-ropes, four branching cords, and untorn stalks; sand for the mounds, flour of unhusked [barley] for the two rauhiṇa cakes, two purifiers made of muñja grass or darbha grass; and having prepared the clarified butter and the sprinkling waters silently—

24.2.7.a.s: brahman pravargyeṇa pracariṣyāmas \\ hotar gharmam abhiṣṭuhi \\ agnīd rauhiṇau puroḍāśāv adhiśraya \ pratiprasthātar vihara \ prastotaḥ sāmāni gāya \\ iti saṃpreṣyati //
24.2.7.a.d: ब्रह्मन् प्रवर्ग्येण प्रचरिष्यामस् \\ होतर् घर्मम् अभिष्टुहि \\ अग्नीद् रौहिणौ पुरोडाशाव् अधिश्रय \ प्रतिप्रस्थातर् विहर \ प्रस्तोतः सामानि गाय \\ इति संप्रेष्यति ॥
24.2.7.a.m: he directs [the priests]: 'Brahman, we shall proceed with the pravargya; hotṛ, praise the gharma; agnīdh, place the two rauhiṇa cakes on the fire; pratiprasthātṛ, spread [the sacrificial fires]; prastotṛ, sing the chants.'

24.2.8.a.s: brahmā yajuryuktam̐ sāmabhir āktakhaṃ tvā \\ ity anudrutya \\ om indravantaḥ pracarata \\ iti prasauti prasūtas \\ yamāya tvā \ makhāya tvā \\ iti sarvaṃ paridharmaṃ triḥ prokṣati //
24.2.8.a.d: ब्रह्मा यजुर्युक्तम्̐ सामभिर् आक्तखं त्वा \\ इत्य् अनुद्रुत्य \\ ओम् इन्द्रवन्तः प्रचरत \\ इति प्रसौति प्रसूतस् \\ यमाय त्वा \ मखाय त्वा \\ इति सर्वं परिधर्मं त्रिः प्रोक्षति ॥
24.2.8.a.m: Having recited, 'Joined with the yajus, [the gharma] whose aperture is smeared with the chants...', the brahman gives permission with, 'Om! Accompanied by Indra, proceed!' Having received permission, he sprinkles all the implements for the gharma three times with, 'For Yama, you,' 'For Makha, you.'

24.2.9.a.s: prokṣitāni pratiprasthātā vyāyātayatīti vijñāyata etasmin kāla āgnīdhras tūṣṇīm upacaritau rauhiṇau puroḍāśāv adhiśrayati //
24.2.9.a.d: प्रोक्षितानि प्रतिप्रस्थाता व्यायातयतीति विज्ञायत एतस्मिन् काल आग्नीध्रस् तूष्णीम् उपचरितौ रौहिणौ पुरोडाशाव् अधिश्रयति ॥
24.2.9.a.m: It is taught that the pratiprasthātṛ arranges in order the sprinkled objects. At this time, the āgnīdhra places the two rauhiṇa cakes, which have been attended to silently, on the fire.

24.2.10.a.s: samrāḍāsandīm agreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya purastād rājāsandyā nidadhāti tasyāṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomāstīrya deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tvā \\ iti tasminn itarau mahāvīrau prāñcāv upaśayau nidadhāti tāv apracaraṇīyau bhavato methīṃ mayūkhān viśākhadāmānīty ādāyāgreṇa hotāraṃ dakṣiṇātikramya dakṣiṇayā dvāropanirvṛtya dakṣiṇena methīṃ nihanti hotuḥ samīkṣāyā etasyā eva pūrvasyā dvāryāyā dakṣiṇato vatsasya śaṅkum etasyā evāparasyā dvāryāyā dakṣiṇato 'jāyā uttarato 'bhyantaraṃ barkarasya teṣu viśākhadāmāni vyāyātayati tān evam eva vyātitāni bhavanty odvāsanāt //
24.2.10.a.d: सम्राडासन्दीम् अग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य पुरस्ताद् राजासन्द्या निदधाति तस्यां कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमास्तीर्य देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वा \\ इति तस्मिन्न् इतरौ महावीरौ प्राञ्चाव् उपशयौ निदधाति ताव् अप्रचरणीयौ भवतो मेथीं मयूखान् विशाखदामानीत्य् आदायाग्रेण होतारं दक्षिणातिक्रम्य दक्षिणया द्वारोपनिर्वृत्य दक्षिणेन मेथीं निहन्ति होतुः समीक्षाया एतस्या एव पूर्वस्या द्वार्याया दक्षिणतो वत्सस्य शङ्कुम् एतस्या एवापरस्या द्वार्याया दक्षिणतो ऽजाया उत्तरतो ऽभ्यन्तरं बर्करस्य तेषु विशाखदामानि व्यायातयति तान् एवम् एव व्यातितानि भवन्त्य् ओद्वासनात् ॥
24.2.10.a.m: Carrying the samrāṭ chair around the front of the āhavanīya fire, he places it east of the rājā chair. Having spread upon it a black-antelope skin with its neck pointing east and the hair upward, with [the mantra], 'O god who goest before, may I be equal to thee,' he places the other two mahāvīra pots facing east as reserve pots on it; they are not used in the performance. Taking the peg, the stakes, and the branched cords, stepping across southward in front of the hotṛ and coming out by the south door, he drives in the peg south of the hotṛ's line of sight; south of this very eastern door-post [he drives in] the calf's stake, south of this very western door-post [that] of the she-goat, and inside to the north [that] of the young kid. Over them he stretches the branched cords; they remain stretched in this very way until the disposal [of the Pravargya apparatus].

24.2.11.a.s: tair enān kāle badhnanty uttareṇa gārhapatyāhavanīyau kharāv upanivapaty uttarapūrvam avāntaradeśaṃ pratyucchiṣṭakharaṃ bāhyato niṣecanavantam uttareṇāhavanīyam̐ śakalān upasādayati kāṇṭakīṃ samidham //
24.2.11.a.d: तैर् एनान् काले बध्नन्त्य् उत्तरेण गार्हपत्याहवनीयौ खराव् उपनिवपत्य् उत्तरपूर्वम् अवान्तरदेशं प्रत्युच्छिष्टखरं बाह्यतो निषेचनवन्तम् उत्तरेणाहवनीयम्̐ शकलान् उपसादयति काण्टकीं समिधम् ॥
24.2.11.a.m: With these they tie them at the [proper] time. To the north of the gārhapatya and āhavanīya fires he scatters two mounds; facing the north-eastern intermediate quarter [he scatters] the mound for the remnants, which has a drainage channel on the outside. To the north of the āhavanīya fire he sets down the wood-chips and the thorny firewood stick.

24.3.1.a.s: ādāya mahāvīraṃ deva puraścara saṃghyāsaṃ tvā \\ ity aparivāsitena vedena saṃmārṣṭi prāṇāya svāhā \ vyānāya svāhā \\ iti sruveṇāhavanīye sapta prāṇāhutīr juhoty ekādaśa vottamasya śeṣeṇa devas tvā savitā madhvānaktu \\ iti mahāvīram anakti taṃ nidhāyānyasmai vā pradāya pṛthivīṃ tapasas trāyasva \\ ity aparasmin khare rājatam̐ rukmaṃ nidhāya dvayān muñjapralavān ādāya \\ arcir asi \\ iti dakṣiṇeṣām agrāṇi gārhapatya ādīpayati śocir asi \\ iti teṣām agrair uttareṣāṃ mūlāni jyotir asi \\ iti teṣāṃ mūlair dakṣiṇeṣāṃ mūlāni tapo 'si \\ iti teṣāṃ mūlair uttareṣām agrāṇi tān vyatyastān upari rukme nidhāya //
24.3.1.a.d: आदाय महावीरं देव पुरश्चर संघ्यासं त्वा \\ इत्य् अपरिवासितेन वेदेन संमार्ष्टि प्राणाय स्वाहा \ व्यानाय स्वाहा \\ इति स्रुवेणाहवनीये सप्त प्राणाहुतीर् जुहोत्य् एकादश वोत्तमस्य शेषेण देवस् त्वा सविता मध्वानक्तु \\ इति महावीरम् अनक्ति तं निधायान्यस्मै वा प्रदाय पृथिवीं तपसस् त्रायस्व \\ इत्य् अपरस्मिन् खरे राजतम्̐ रुक्मं निधाय द्वयान् मुञ्जप्रलवान् आदाय \\ अर्चिर् असि \\ इति दक्षिणेषाम् अग्राणि गार्हपत्य आदीपयति शोचिर् असि \\ इति तेषाम् अग्रैर् उत्तरेषां मूलानि ज्योतिर् असि \\ इति तेषां मूलैर् दक्षिणेषां मूलानि तपो ऽसि \\ इति तेषां मूलैर् उत्तरेषाम् अग्राणि तान् व्यत्यस्तान् उपरि रुक्मे निधाय ॥
24.3.1.a.m: Taking the mahāvīra pot, with [the mantra], 'O god who goest before, may I be equal to thee,' he wipes it with an untrimmed veda grass bunch. With the sruva, with [the formulas], 'To the in-breath, svāhā! To the diffused breath, svāhā!' he offers seven, or eleven, prāṇa oblations into the āhavanīya fire. With the remainder of the last oblation, with [the mantra], 'May the god Savitṛ anoint thee with honey,' he anoints the mahāvīra pot. Having set it down, or having handed it over to another, with [the mantra], 'Protect the earth from heat,' he places a silver plate on the western mound; having taken two bunches of muñja reed-tops, with [the formula], 'Thou art the flame,' he ignites the tips of those to the south in the gārhapatya fire; with [the formula], 'Thou art the glow,' [he ignites] with their tips the roots of those to the north; with [the formula], 'Thou art the light,' with their roots the roots of those to the south; with [the formula], 'Thou art the heat,' with their roots the tips of those to the north. Having placed them crosswise upon the plate,

24.3.2.a.s: sam̐sīdasva \\ iti teṣu mahāvīram̐ sādayati \\ añjanti \\ ity ājyenānakty abhimantrayate vā \\ anādhṛṣyā purastād ity etaiḥ pratimantraṃ pratidiśam asam̐spṛśan yajamāno mahāvīraṃ prāñcaṃ prādeśaṃ dhārayati manor aśvāsi bhūriputrā \\ ity uttarataḥ pṛthivīm abhimṛśati //
24.3.2.a.d: सम्̐सीदस्व \\ इति तेषु महावीरम्̐ सादयति \\ अञ्जन्ति \\ इत्य् आज्येनानक्त्य् अभिमन्त्रयते वा \\ अनाधृष्या पुरस्ताद् इत्य् एतैः प्रतिमन्त्रं प्रतिदिशम् असम्̐स्पृशन् यजमानो महावीरं प्राञ्चं प्रादेशं धारयति मनोर् अश्वासि भूरिपुत्रा \\ इत्य् उत्तरतः पृथिवीम् अभिमृशति ॥
24.3.2.a.m: with [the mantra], 'Sit down together,' he places the mahāvīra pot upon them. With [the mantra], 'They anoint...,' he anoints [it] with clarified butter, or consecrates [it]. With the [mantras beginning], 'Invincible from the east...,' [recited] mantra by mantra for each cardinal direction, without touching [it], the sacrificer holds a span [above] the eastward-facing mahāvīra pot. With [the mantra], 'Thou art Manu's mare, mother of many sons,' he touches the earth to the north.

24.3.3.a.s: siddhyai tvā \\ iti dhṛṣṭī ādāyādhvaryuḥ pratiprasthātā ca tapo ṣv agne \\ iti gārhapatyād udīco 'ṅgārān niruhya citaḥ stha paricitas \\ iti pradakṣiṇam aṅgārair mahāvīraṃ paryuhya vaikaṅkataiḥ paridhibhiḥ paridhattas \\ mā asi \\ iti prāñcāv adhvaryur nidadhāti / pramā asi \\ ity udañcau pratiprasthātā / evam eva pūrveṇādhvaryur uttareṇa pratiprasthātā / antarikṣasyāntardhir asi \\ ity adhvaryur eva trayodaśaṃ dakṣiṇato nidadhāti //
24.3.3.a.d: सिद्ध्यै त्वा \\ इति धृष्टी आदायाध्वर्युः प्रतिप्रस्थाता च तपो ष्व् अग्ने \\ इति गार्हपत्याद् उदीचो ऽङ्गारान् निरुह्य चितः स्थ परिचितस् \\ इति प्रदक्षिणम् अङ्गारैर् महावीरं पर्युह्य वैकङ्कतैः परिधिभिः परिधत्तस् \\ मा असि \\ इति प्राञ्चाव् अध्वर्युर् निदधाति । प्रमा असि \\ इत्य् उदञ्चौ प्रतिप्रस्थाता । एवम् एव पूर्वेणाध्वर्युर् उत्तरेण प्रतिप्रस्थाता । अन्तरिक्षस्यान्तर्धिर् असि \\ इत्य् अध्वर्युर् एव त्रयोदशं दक्षिणतो निदधाति ॥
24.3.3.a.m: With [the formula], 'For success, thee,' the adhvaryu and the pratiprasthātā taking the two tongs, with [the mantra], 'Heat well, O Agni,' drawing out burning coals towards the north from the gārhapatya fire, with [the mantra], 'Piled up are ye, heaped around,' piling the burning coals around the mahāvīra pot clockwise, they enclose it with encircling sticks of vikankata wood. With [the formula], 'Thou art the measure,' the adhvaryu places two facing east; with [the formula], 'Thou art the counterpart,' the pratiprasthātā [places] two facing north; in this very manner the adhvaryu [places two] to the east and the pratiprasthātā to the north. With [the formula], 'Thou art the cover of the intermediate space,' the adhvaryu alone places the thirteenth to the south.

24.3.4.a.s: mahāvīra ājyam ānīya divaṃ tapasas trāyasva \\ ity upariṣṭāt sauvarṇena rukmeṇāpidhāya \\ ābhir gīrbhir iti tisṛbhir upatiṣṭhate dhavitrāṇy ādatte gāyatram asi \\ iti prathamam \\ traiṣṭubham asi \\ iti dvitīyam \\ jāgatam asi \\ iti tṛtīyaṃ tair enam ūrdhvaṃ tribhir dhūnoti madhu madhu \\ iti teṣām ekam agnīdhe prayacchaty ekaṃ pratiprasthātre ta āgnīdhraprathamās triḥ pradakṣiṇam ūrdhvaṃ dhūnvanto mahāvīraṃ pariyanti madhu madhu \\ iti praṇavena sam̐rādhayantīti vijñāyate //
24.3.4.a.d: महावीर आज्यम् आनीय दिवं तपसस् त्रायस्व \\ इत्य् उपरिष्टात् सौवर्णेन रुक्मेणापिधाय \\ आभिर् गीर्भिर् इति तिसृभिर् उपतिष्ठते धवित्राण्य् आदत्ते गायत्रम् असि \\ इति प्रथमम् \\ त्रैष्टुभम् असि \\ इति द्वितीयम् \\ जागतम् असि \\ इति तृतीयं तैर् एनम् ऊर्ध्वं त्रिभिर् धूनोति मधु मधु \\ इति तेषाम् एकम् अग्नीधे प्रयच्छत्य् एकं प्रतिप्रस्थात्रे त आग्नीध्रप्रथमास् त्रिः प्रदक्षिणम् ऊर्ध्वं धून्वन्तो महावीरं परियन्ति मधु मधु \\ इति प्रणवेन सम्̐राधयन्तीति विज्ञायते ॥
24.3.4.a.m: Pouring clarified butter into the mahāvīra pot, covering it from above with a golden plate with [the mantra], 'Protect the sky from heat,' he attends upon [it] with the three [verses beginning], 'With these songs...'. He takes the fanning-fans: the first with [the formula], 'Thou art the Gāyatra'; the second with [the formula], 'Thou art the Traiṣṭubha'; the third with [the formula], 'Thou art the Jāgata'. Upwards, with the three, he fans it, [whispering], 'Sweetness! Sweetness!' He gives one of them to the āgnīdhra, one to the pratiprasthātā. Led by the āgnīdhra, fanning upwards, they go around the mahāvīra pot clockwise three times, [whispering], 'Sweetness! Sweetness!' It is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: 'They propitiate it with the syllable oṃ.'

24.3.5.a.s: yathālokam upaviśya samañjata indhānā āsate prajvalite rukmam apādatta iti vijñāyate //
24.3.5.a.d: यथालोकम् उपविश्य समञ्जत इन्धाना आसते प्रज्वलिते रुक्मम् अपादत्त इति विज्ञायते ॥
24.3.5.a.m: Having sat down according to their places, they sit rekindling [the fire] together. When it has flared up, he takes off the plate, so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

24.3.6.a.s: yābhir vartikāṃ grasitām amuñcatam ity ucyamāne daśa prācīr daśa bhāsi dakṣiṇā \\ ity etam anuvākaṃ yajamānaṃ vācayati \\ apnasvatīm aśvinā vācam asme ity ucyamāne rucito gharmas \\ ity upottiṣṭhann āha yathetaṃ trir anabhidhūnvantaḥ pratipariyanti //
24.3.6.a.d: याभिर् वर्तिकां ग्रसिताम् अमुञ्चतम् इत्य् उच्यमाने दश प्राचीर् दश भासि दक्षिणा \\ इत्य् एतम् अनुवाकं यजमानं वाचयति \\ अप्नस्वतीम् अश्विना वाचम् अस्मे इत्य् उच्यमाने रुचितो घर्मस् \\ इत्य् उपोत्तिष्ठन्न् आह यथेतं त्रिर् अनभिधून्वन्तः प्रतिपरियन्ति ॥
24.3.6.a.m: While [the verse], 'By which [aids] ye freed the swallowed quail...,' is being recited, he makes the sacrificer recite this anuvāka: 'Ten [are] east, ten thou shinest south...'. While [the verse], 'Bringing wealth, O Aśvins, speech unto us...,' is being recited, rising up, he says, 'The gharma has shone.' Without fanning, they walk back around three times as they had come.

24.3.7.a.s: tasmin kāle pratiprasthātā pratyetya dhavitrāṇy ādāyāgreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya samrāḍāsandyāṃ nidadhāti svāhā tvā sūryasya raśmibhyas \\ iti prātaḥ svāhā tvā nakṣatrebhyas \\ iti sāyaṃ yathālokam upotthāya \\ apaśyaṃ gopām iti sarva ṛtvijo yajamānaś cādhīyanto mahāvīram avekṣante tvaṣṭīmatī te sapeya \\ iti pariśrite pratiprasthātā patnīṃ vācayati //
24.3.7.a.d: तस्मिन् काले प्रतिप्रस्थाता प्रत्येत्य धवित्राण्य् आदायाग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य सम्राडासन्द्यां निदधाति स्वाहा त्वा सूर्यस्य रश्मिभ्यस् \\ इति प्रातः स्वाहा त्वा नक्षत्रेभ्यस् \\ इति सायं यथालोकम् उपोत्थाय \\ अपश्यं गोपाम् इति सर्व ऋत्विजो यजमानश् चाधीयन्तो महावीरम् अवेक्षन्ते त्वष्टीमती ते सपेय \\ इति परिश्रिते प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्नीं वाचयति ॥
24.3.7.a.m: At that time the pratiprasthātā, returning, taking the fanning-fans and carrying them around in front of the āhavanīya fire, places them on the samrāṭ chair.
